News.title: UK sees hottest day of the year as 38.1C recorded in Kew Gardens
News.content:
The UK has experienced its hottest day of the year and fifth hottest day on record, as a heatwave that gripped much of the country peaked at 38.1C on Thursday, the Met Office said.

Kew Gardens in west London recorded England's top temperature, provisionally surpassing the 38C recorded in Lingwood, Norfolk on 26 June.

The latest spell of extreme heat marks the UK's fifth heatwave this year, with the Met Office warning this summer is on course to be the UK's hottest since records began.

An amber heat health alert, warning of significant detrimental impacts to health and social care services is in place across the whole of England until 21:00 BST on Friday.

News.title: Five key takeaways from results day 2026
News.content:
Results for A-levels, T-levels, BTecs and other vocational qualifications are out.

And this year, they've come at a time when all eyes are on what teenagers decide to do next.

Universities are keen to get them through the door. As they grapple with their finances, they know that every filled seat in a lecture hall comes with tuition fee funding.

The new prime minister, meanwhile, wants to carve out clear routes into technical jobs that can rival the well-established path of A-levels and a university degree.

For teenagers, considerations about the immediate and long-term cost of university, as well as the availability of other options, are all in the mix.

Here are the standout things you need to know.

News.title: Son of 102-year-old says father died after being 'pushed off stage'
News.content:
Robert said: "He just asked them to turn the music down."

He said his father turned around to come back down off the stage when he was pushed, and that resulted in a broken hip.

"[That's] the most upsetting part. He wasn't going to live forever but it's not a nice way, obviously in pain," he said.

"We want to see justice, of course.

"They must have known he was an old man. It makes you wonder what the world is coming to.

"It has obviously made it difficult. It would've been nice if he'd gone quietly in his sleep.

"He was in hospital, suffering, for a week-and-a-half. It's not nice.

"I feel sad - even though he could be difficult because of his age and dementia, still, you get used to him being around," he said.

Robert, a retired civil engineer, said his father used to visit the Crow's Nest.

"What happened is not nice. The pub has changed a lot over the years. It has become a youngsters' pub," he said.

Robert said he grew up in the home in the the Llanyrafon neighbourhood where his father had lived since 1960.

He said his dad had a career as a design draughtsman and had lived alone since his wife died 40 years ago.

"Me and my brother would visit our father regularly, and clean the house and buy him food.

"His eyesight had deteriorated and he had been diagnosed with dementia two or three years ago."

Robert said: "He's well-known around here, although a lot of his generation are gone," he added.

He said his father would visit the pub two or three times a week, where he would drink beers, and described how he became a familiar face to some locals.

"I suppose he became a pub character," he added.

News.title: The key signs you may have damaged your eyes by looking at the eclipse
News.content:
Eye experts are warning people to be on the alert for any signs their vision has been damaged by looking at the sun during Wednesday's eclipse.

The symptoms can include blurred vision, a central blind or dark spot and increased sensitivity to light.

After the previous total eclipse of the sun that was visible in the UK in 1999, around 70 people were left with damaged sight.

Many of them had spent less than a minute looking at the spectacle, without realising they were harming their eyes.

The danger comes because staring at an eclipse without protection can damage the retina, which sits at the back of the eye, and particularly those cells responsible for sharp central vision.

The sun is incredibly bright, even when partially obscured by the moon.

Normally if we stare at it, we wince and quickly look away.

But when it is darker, during an eclipse, that instinct may not kick in, even while our eyes are being damaged.

The bright light and ultraviolet radiation given off by the sun can lead to a condition known as "solar retinopathy".

And because the retina has no pain receptors, it's hard for people to notice the damage as it happens, so symptoms may only appear several hours later.

Leading up to the eclipse itself, experts were warning only genuine specially-designed solar eclipse glasses should be used, and that ordinary sunglasses or other devices were not enough to prevent potential damage.

News.title: Honeytrap thieves jailed for killing men they had drugged
News.content:
A couple who drugged men seeking sexual services in order to steal from them have been jailed for killing two men and poisoning others.

Adina Mihai and Madalin Dumitru admitted the manslaughter of Gary Mouat, 37, from Oxfordshire, and Malcolm King, 80, from Gloucestershire, in 2025 and 2024 respectively.

On the first day of their trial in June, the pair also each admitted two further counts of administering poison to surviving victims.

Mihai, 31, and Dumitru, 30, were both sentenced to 17 years in prison at Oxford Crown Court.

Mihai, who posed as a sex worker, and her partner Dumitru, arranged to meet men paying for services she had advertised online at their homes.

The court heard four had their alcoholic drinks spiked with the powerful sedative gamma-butyrolactone (GBL) so the pair could steal from them.

Two men died as a result, while two others - who cannot be named due to reporting restrictions - survived.

News.title: Bonnie Tyler's classic hit spiked in streams during solar eclipse
News.content:
Born Gaynor Hopkins in a council house in Neath, Tyler grew up with a love for music before she was discovered by talent scout Roger Bell in a Swansea club.

Tyler released her first single, Lost in France in 1977, but it was the release of Total Eclipse of the Heart five years later which changed her life.

The ballad spent two weeks at UK number one and four weeks in the US.

The iconic love song's music video surpassed 1.2 billion views on YouTube and has had over a billion streams on Spotify.

Spotify previously said it had paid out more than $1.4 million for streams of Tyler's catalogue in 2025.

The music platform said Total Eclipse of the Heart was one of a few "celestial" songs that saw a streaming spike in the UK on 12 August.

According to Spotify, the biggest increases in UK streams during the eclipse were:

Evolfo, Moon Eclipsed the Sun (+12,817%)

Chris Staples, Dark Side of the Moon (+2,805%)

Pink Floyd, Eclipse (+594%)

Delta Goodrem, Eclipse (+104%)

Bonnie Tyler, Total Eclipse of the Heart (+94%)

Bill Withers, Ain't No Sunshine (+17%)

Shannon Carragher, senior editor at Spotify, said: "It is always fascinating to see how major cultural events instantly reflect in what the UK is listening to.

"Cultural phenomena like the solar eclipse naturally bring people together and we instinctively look for the perfect soundtrack to share that moment."

Ahead of the solar eclipse, Tyler's McVitie's Jaffa Cakes TV advert also resurfaced - it was originally broadcast in 2023 when there was a partial lunar eclipse.

The nostalgic advert came after research revealed almost half (49%) of Brits did not understand how eclipses occurred.

In the video, Tyler uses a Jaffa Cake as a prop to describe the different types of eclipse.

She said: "There are three types of eclipse. You've got the lunar eclipse, the solar eclipse, and then there's the total eclipse of the heart.

"When the earth is situated between the moon and the sun it creates a shadow, and when it looks like someone has just taken a bite out of the moon. That's a partial lunar eclipse."

The grammy-nominated star had a string of other hits, including Holding out for a Hero and also represented the UK at the Eurovision Song Contest in 2013.

She was named in the Queen's last Birthday Honours list in 2022 and was awarded an MBE for her services to music by Prince William the following year.

Tyler died "unexpectedly" on 8 July, aged 75, at a Portugal hospital, "as a result of the illness that she was being treated for", her family said in a statement released on the star's official website, external.

At the time, tributes poured in from a host of friends and stars including Catherine Zeta-Jones, Bryan Adams and Rod Stewart.

Tyler's funeral service will take place on 17 August at 12:00 BST at St Mary's Church in Swansea.

It has since been confirmed that her coffin will be brought to her Mumbles home on 15 August at 15:30 BST.

People are invited to "pay their respects" by lining Newton Road at 15:15 BST.

News.title: How to get a good night's sleep during hot weather
News.content:
Hot weather can make you feel tired and lethargic during the day.

That is because you are using more energy to regulate your internal temperature.

But if your sleep is disturbed at night, try to avoid napping during the day.

When it is hot, feeling sleepy can be precious - save it for bedtime.

News.title: Six ways to keep your home and yourself cool in hot weather
News.content:
Tepid showers can help to cool your body temperature, saving both money and energy. But Prof Tipton warns not to go too cold: "The trick is to try and get the skin as cool as possible whilst maintaining maximum blood flow to it.

"Too cold and the body will shut down blood to the skin and trap the heat in the body making it harder to get out."

Putting an ice pack or cold-water bottle on your body can achieve an instant feeling of relief. You may want to wrap it in a towel to avoid direct contact with your skin.

Your clothes can also really affect your body temperature.

Natural fibres like cotton and linen help to regulate body temperature and loose-fitting clothing allows room for the breeze to cool you down.

This is also why cotton bed sheets can help you sleep when hot air fills a room.

News.title: Big Issue says vendors struggling as sales hit by heatwaves
News.content:
Big Issue vendors are struggling to sell magazines in the UK's extreme heat, which is having an "immediate" impact on their earnings, Big Issue's managing director says.

Sales of the British news and entertainment magazine are down on average 20% year on year in weeks where heatwaves have been declared, Catherine Parsons said.

During June's record-breaking temperatures, the worst-hit West Midlands and Wales saw 34% and 33% fewer sales respectively.

George Anderson, who sells the Big Issue near the BBC's Broadcasting House in London, says it is a struggle when footfall is lower and people would rather be near the aircon.

"People are uncomfortable, they don't want to hang around in the heat and chat," he told the BBC on the hottest day of the year.

"I manage it as best I can, and so far so good, but my sales are definitely down which can be quite tough."

Big Issue is sold by people experiencing homelessness or financial instability.

But Parsons said sellers are losing out on vital income due to the heatwaves.

"For most of us, extreme heat is an inconvenience. For Big Issue vendors, it means earning significantly less and making difficult decisions about rent, food and other essentials," she said.

In the week of 22 June, when the UK's June temperature record was broken and temperatures hit 37.7C (99.9F), Big Issue sales fell by an average of 22% compared to the same week the previous year, their figures show.

The latest spell of extreme heat marks the UK's fifth heatwave this year, with the Met Office warning this summer is on course to be the UK's hottest since records began.

Parsons said Big Issue teams were working to support vendors and had been handing out sunscreen, caps and water bottles.

"But in the most extreme temperatures, it's simply unsafe for vendors to be out and selling, and when the heat forces them to cut their working day short, the financial impact is immediate."

News.title: Dad to stand trial accused of murdering daughter Minnie Merriman
News.content:
The father of a nine-year-old girl who died after being found seriously injured at an industrial estate in Arbroath is to stand trial accused of her murder.

Prosecutors allege Christopher Rice, from Wakefield, West Yorkshire, killed Minnie Merriman, who died in Dundee's Ninewells Hospital on 3 August.

The 35-year-old, who was remanded in custody, made no plea during a second appearance in private via videolink at Forfar Sheriff Court. He was fully committed for trial.

Minnie's family previously paid tribute to their "beloved, absolutely incredible, beautiful and brave Minnie Moo".

Emergency services were called to the Elliot Industrial Estate in Arbroath shortly after midnight on 3 August following reports that a child had been found injured.

Minnie was taken to Ninewells Hospital alongside four other people, but later died as a result of her injuries.

Police Scotland said they were not looking for anyone else in connection with Minnie's death and the other members of the family - who were camping in the area - are being supported by specialist officers.

News.title: Second attempted murder arrest after cycle path attack
News.content:
A second suspect has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after a man was attacked on the Bristol to Bath Railway Path.

The victim, aged in his 30s, was taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries believed to have been caused by a "bladed weapon" following the incident near Bitton at about 20:00 BST on Tuesday.

One teenager was arrested on the night of the attack and a second was arrested on Wednesday afternoon.

Both have been released on conditional bail while enquiries continue.

Insp Barny Mabbett, from Avon and Somerset Police, said: "Uniformed officers are conducting patrols along the railway path to provide reassurance because we recognise an incident like this does inevitably causes concern.

"Our investigation into what happened is ongoing, but we are also working with other organisations around making sure the railway path is a safe place for people to enjoy and use both in the short-term and long-term."

News.title: Leicester City put up for sale for more than £200m
News.content:
Leicester City are looking to sell the club for more than Â£200m, with its Thai owners King Power ready to leave after 16 years.

The Foxes have had an eight-page sales booklet produced by a leading US investment bank to help offload the one-time Premier League title winners.

Citigroup lists the Foxes, its women's team, and other major assets - including the 32,000-seat King Power Stadium and its Seagrave training facility which was opened in 2020 and is valued at Â£121m - as well as OH Leuven, Leicester's Belgian sister club, as up for sale in a brochure titled 'Project Lineup'.

The document, seen by BBC Sport, values the club's physical assets at more than Â£200m, though no specific sum has been attributed to the sale of its struggling teams.

The brochure speaks of "a rare opportunity to acquire a club with an excellent track record of winning promotions to higher divisions".

Leicester's successes, including the 5,000-1 Premier League title win of 2016 and the FA Cup triumph five years later, are well promoted in the brochure, while their place in League One, after back-to-back relegations from the top flight and the Championship, fail to get a mention.

The club's turnover, which Citigroup forecast to be more than Â£97m for the 2026 financial year are also part of the pitch, but the years of financial losses and the club's debts - which, as outlined in its 2025 accounts, include Â£103.6m in bank loans - are omitted.

In the years that the club yo-yoed between the Premier League and Championship, with two relegations from the top flight in three years between 2023 and 2025, the club lost more than Â£180m.

News.title: Bishop appears in court over child rape charges
News.content:
A 70-year-old bishop has appeared in court for the first time accused of two counts of rape against a female under the age of 16.

David Oakley, the Bishop of Northampton, was charged in June following an investigation by Staffordshire Police.

He appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court via videolink from his lawyer's office.

Oakley was not asked to enter a plea during the hearing as Chief Magistrate Paul Goldspring sent the case to the Old Bailey.

Oakley was released on bail, with conditions not to contact the alleged victim, or her family, ahead of a plea hearing on 10 September.

The incidents allegedly took place in Staffordshire between February 2000 and February 2001, when Oakley was in his mid-40s working as a Catholic priest.

Oakley was born in Stourbridge, West Midlands, and ordained as a priest in 1980 before becoming Bishop of Northampton in 2020.

Oakley retains the title of Bishop but has withdrawn from public ministry.

The Catholic Diocese of Northampton - which covers Northamptonshire, Bedfordshire and Buckinghamshire â said in a previous statement that it recognised the case was "very distressing for all concerned".

News.title: Human bones found in south-east London garden
News.content:
Human bones found in the garden of a bungalow in south-east London are being examined by the Met Police.

Officers were called to Aperfield Road in Biggin Hill at about 15:30 BST last Friday, the force said.

The bones were sent for specialist examination which confirmed they were human. They are now undergoing further tests to establish their age and identity, police added.

The area around the home was cordoned off for six days, according to The Sun, external, with one resident telling the newspaper the property was being renovated.

"The builders discovered something on Friday and of course they completely had to stop work," they added.

A Metropolitan Police spokesperson added: "The crime scene is now closed and an investigation remains ongoing to establish the full circumstances."

News.title: Ski Sunday host Chemmy Alcott suffers collapsed lung after jumping into lake
News.content:
Ski Sunday presenter Chemmy Alcott says she suffered a collapsed lung after jumping into a lake while on holiday in France.

The 44-year-old former GB Olympic skier posted a clip on Instagram, external that showed her jumping off a five metre platform into Lake Annecy, in the French Alps, before landing badly and ending up in hospital.

"Most people badly time a front flip off a five-metre platform and get winded," she said in the clip.

"I apparently don't do things by halves. Collapsed lung, chest drain and a very expensive lesson in rotation."

Alcott explained that she initially went back to jump again after her difficult landing, out of "embarassment" and "just so I wasn't making a big deal out of it".

But she soon realised she "couldn't breathe properly and should probably go and get it checked out".

She later shared images of herself in hospital with tubes and wires sticking out of her body.

In the caption to the main clip - titled "this didn't end well" - she wrote: "Well... that escalated quickly. Turns out five metres is quite a long way to discover you've got the rotation wrong.

"One badly timed front flip. One very hard landing. One collapsed lung. One chest drain. And a few more hospital overnights than were on the holiday itinerary...

"I absolutely loved Annecyâ¦ but I'm not entirely sure it loved me back."

A collapsed lung - medically known as a pneumothorax - occurs when air becomes trapped in the space between the lung and the chest wall, according the NHS.

News.title: UK economy grows but experts warn of challenging months ahead
News.content:
Summer sun and sports fixtures helped the UK economy grow between April and June, according to official data, but some economists warned the outlook for the rest of the year was weaker.

The economy expanded by 0.4%, in line with market expectations but below a 0.6% increase in the first three months of this year.

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said growth had "remained relatively robust", with the UK ahead of other G7 countries for growth this year so far.

Experts questioned whether this resilience would be maintained, however, given growth was fuelled by some temporary factors and energy prices could remain volatile if the Middle East conflict continues.

The British economy is now 1.2% bigger than a year ago, the ONS said, despite fears that the Iran war, which started at the end of February, and politically uncertainty around Sir Keir Starmer's resignation as prime minister would hold back growth.

Between April and June, sectors including computer programming, advertising and the pharmaceutical industry lifted growth. That was offset by falls in power generation and sewerage.

The ONS said some businesses reported that "good weather and sporting events may have had a positive effect" in June, boosting month-on-month growth to 0.3%.

The men's football World Cup, which kicked off mid-June, increased customers at hospitality venues showing the matches.

June also saw several of summer's heatwaves. However, May's growth was revised down from 0.1% to zero growth.

Six Flags Magic Mountain’s X2, considered one of the world’s most extreme roller coasters, has been shut down for over a month following an incident in which a rider was reportedly found unconscious.

The Los Angeles County Fire Department responded to the Valencia, California, theme park around 9:15 p.m. on July 5 after receiving a report of an unconscious person, KTLA reported Wednesday. Park medical personnel also responded and helped handle the situation alongside firefighters.

The incident was handled at the scene and did not result in a sheriff’s investigation, according to the LA County Sheriff’s Department, the outlet reports.

Further details about the incident remain unclear. Six Flags has not publicly addressed what happened, only telling KTLA that “the ride remains closed at this time.”

The news outlet could not independently confirm the rider’s condition on Wednesday.

open image in gallery The X2 roller coaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain (park overview pictured) has been closed since July 5 following an incident involving an unconscious rider, KTLA reports ( Getty )

The California Division of Occupational Safety and Health, known as Cal/OSHA, also responded to the incident. The agency oversees theme park rides and can inspect attractions following major modifications, as well as in response to complaints, accidents and other safety concerns.

A Cal/OSHA representative told KTLA: “Cal/OSHA’s Amusement Ride and Tramway Unit has opened an inspection into the reported incident involving the X2 roller coaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain. Because the inspection is ongoing, no further details are available at this time.”

The Independent has contacted Six Flags and Cal/OSHA for comment.

X2 is the world’s first “fourth-dimensional” roller coaster that spins riders in their seats while the train navigates steep drops and inversions along its 3,600-foot track at speeds of up to 76 mph. Originally opened as X in 2002, the ride was upgraded and relaunched as X2 in 2008, becoming the final coaster designed and built by the famous engineering company Arrow Dynamics.

The latest incident isn’t the first time X2 has faced serious scrutiny. Six Flags is also fighting a lawsuit from the family of Christopher Hawley, 22, who they say suffered a fatal brain injury on the coaster in June 2022, according to KTLA. A jury trial is scheduled to begin in September.

According to the lawsuit, X2 “suddenly, abruptly and violently jolted to a halt” as Hawley, his younger brother and cousin approached the end of the ride. After exiting, Hawley appeared unsteady and complained that his head hurt before collapsing and losing consciousness.

Hawley was rushed to Henry Mayo Newhall Hospital, where doctors found a catastrophic subdural hematoma that his family alleges was caused by the ride. He died the following day.

Six Flags has declined to comment on the lawsuit, citing the ongoing litigation, KTLA reports.

President Donald Trump has long blamed vandals for the persistent problems plaguing the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, including algae blooms and peeling paint. Now, Scooby-Doo and his team of mystery investigators are on the case — at least in a newly released parody video.

Posted online Wednesday, the video spoofs an episode of the animated series while skewering Trump, whose administration recently acknowledged that a botched renovation was responsible for the pool’s problems.

Created by Jason Moore, an Ohio-based graphic artist, the video has drawn more than one million views on Facebook, and tens of thousands more across YouTube and TikTok.

The clip opens with Trump summoning Scooby-Doo, Shaggy, Daphne, Fred and Velma to the Oval Office. “Somebody, very bad people, turned my beautiful pool green: vandals,” the president says before enlisting the gang to “solve the mystery behind it.”

The group heads to the Reflecting Pool in search of clues. There, Shaggy and Scooby-Doo encounter the “Potomac Muck Man,” who chases them while Velma investigates the pool itself. The gang then uses “decoy unredacted Epstein files” to lure the monster into a trap.

open image in gallery A graphic artist created a parody Scooby-Doo episode where President Donald Trump enlists the Mystery gang to solve the case of the Reflecting Pool ( Midnight Oil Productions, YouTube )

After the creature is caught in a net, Fred embraces the urban legend that it had long haunted the grounds. But Velma — who earlier discovered peeled paint, a ripped section of liner and a rushed no-bid contract to repair the pool — ultimately cracks the case.

“There were never any vandals,” says Velma, Mystery Inc.’s most analytical member. “The dark paint made the perfect conditions for this whole debacle, and the contractors botched the job, which led to the liner peeling itself.”

She removes the Muck Man’s mask to reveal that the culprit is the Republican president.

“He played the Muck Man and made up the whole vandal story to scare everyone off before they figured out he was responsible for the whole thing,” she says.

open image in gallery In the video, the gang uses 'decoy unredacted Epstein files' to lure the villain in to be captured ( Midnight Oil Productions/YouTube )

Trump then delivers the franchise’s signature line: “And I would've gotten away with it too if it weren’t for you meddling kids.” Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, responds: “Oh, you’re going to get away with it. We’ll see to that.”

The roughly three-minute clip — which quickly went viral — drew thousands of comments across various platforms, with many viewers praising it for its uncanny resemblance to an original Scooby-Doo episode.

“I somehow missed this one when I was a kid,” wrote one YouTube user, while another chimed in: “This story has all the bells and whistles of a classic Scooby-Doo episode.”

“I am not an AI fan, but this deserved a 'like,’” wrote a third user.

Moore, who identifies as an independent, told The Independent that the Reflecting Pool saga is representative of “the absurdity” taking place in Washington, D.C.

“I thought Scooby-Doo would be a good way to put a highlighter on it,” he said. “And regardless of what side of the political fence you're on, you can have a little laugh and be entertained at the same time.”

Moore — who has created numerous political satire videos — said the project took roughly 50 hours to complete, including scriptwriting and using AI to assist with video production.

The spoof comes as the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool remains at the center of political controversy.

open image in gallery 'He played the muck man and made up the whole vandal story to scare everyone off before they figured out he was responsible for the whole thing,' Velma says of Trump in the video ( Midnight Oil Productions, YouTube )

In April, the Trump administration launched a restoration project intended to spruce up the landmark ahead of America’s 250th birthday in July. The work included applying an “American flag blue” sealant to the pool’s basin.

But the project — carried out under a no-bid contract awarded to a Trump-linked firm and ultimately costing about $16 million — ran into trouble almost immediately. Algae turned the water green, while pieces of the blue coating began floating to the surface.

Officials tried a series of remedies: pouring bleach into the water, vacuuming up algae and, eventually, draining the pool and erecting fencing to allow for additional repairs.

The 80-year-old president, without providing evidence, blamed vandalism for the damage, and several people were arrested at the site, including Olympic canoeist David Hearn — who appears in the parody video as a scapegoat.

Earlier this month, however, the government dropped its charges against Hearn and several others in connection to the pool. Pirro’s office said that, in light of new information released by the Interior Department, “it is difficult to attribute the widespread damage to the Reflecting Pool to vandalism, let alone to establish that fact beyond a reasonable doubt.” The office instead blamed a “botched installation” by contractors.

Trump quickly voiced frustration with Pirro’s decision, telling reporters on Aug. 3: “Frankly, I think she choked.”

A court order that struck down regulations on firearm suppressors and certain guns took effect Thursday after the U.S. Justice Department did not file an appeal before a seven-day deadline set by a federal judge in Texas.

The ruling allows people to purchase silencers, short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns and certain other firearms without registration, while also removing an extra layer of background checks.

The order benefits parties that brought the lawsuit, including some dealers based outside northern Texas, but it is not a national injunction. Advocates say there are similar challenges in federal courts in other states. Separately, some states have their own prohibitions on silencers.

U.S. District Judge James Hendrix in Lubbock, Texas, said regulations in a 1930s-era law are unconstitutional. He said the rules must fall after the Republican-controlled Congress and President Donald Trump eliminated a $200 permit tax on the devices.

Hendrix said his Aug. 5 order would take effect in seven days unless the government appealed. There was no sign of a filing Wednesday in online entries at Hendrix's court or the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals.

The government’s refusal to pursue an immediate appeal “is a failure to defend public safety,” said Emma Brown, executive director at Giffords, the gun violence prevention group.

An email Thursday seeking comment from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, which enforces the law, was not immediately answered. Under court procedure, the government still could file an appeal in the weeks ahead, even while Hendrix's order stands.

Gun Owners of America said two members acquired suppressors at Silencer Shop in Leander, Texas, without having to register.

“Our members are putting the historic victory into action. The era of federal registration for constitutionally protected arms must end,” said Erich Pratt, the group's senior vice president.

The National Firearms Act has been around since 1934 in response to concerns about mafia violence. It regulates firearms that are considered the most dangerous, though gun-rights advocates say it conflicts with the Constitution's Second Amendment.

“The system of regulating these weapons has been effective. The need is no less today than it was after the Prohibition era almost a century ago,” said Giffords chief counsel Adam Skaggs.

Twenty people were injured, two of them seriously, when a train was derailed in East Sussex.

Police declared a major incident after three carriages derailed and toppled onto their sides, leaving a number of people trapped inside in scorching temperatures.

The accident, at 3.44pm on Thursday, involved a Southern Railway train travelling from London Victoria to Eastbourne with around 150 people on board. The carriages derailed near Lewes station.

open image in gallery British Transport Police and rail workers at the scene in East Sussex ( AFP/Getty )

A passenger in one of the carriages said the experience was “completely terrifying”.

“There was a banging. Everything just went topsy-turvy,” said 56-year-old Yana Ludwig, from the United States.

“It seemed like a really long time but it probably was 10 seconds of that before the carriage actually fell on the side.”

She described being propped up over the top of another passenger, and added: “I’m pretty banged up.”

Another passenger told how the carriage “jumped vertically upwards” as it derailed.

open image in gallery Buckled tracks after the derailment ( BBC )

“We felt the train speeding up and starting to rock, and at that point we knew something was very strange, and then our carriage actually jumped vertically upwards, and we could tell there was a derailment,” he told the BBC.

Another passenger said he saw people who were injured.

“There were a number of people in ambulances that had had bad head injuries, and there was visible signs of blood on their heads and, you know, down their clothing,” he said.

Ambulance crews, air ambulances, critical care paramedics, fire crews and police all rushed to the scene.

The people who were trapped were later rescued, British Transport Police said.

open image in gallery Emergency services worked from an adjacent field ( PA Media )

Ms Ludwig estimated it was 20 minutes before the emergency services arrived, adding it seemed like a difficult place for them to reach.

She said everyone on the train was checking their fellow passengers were OK, adding: “These moments everybody kind of pulls together.”

The Rail Accident Investigation Branch sent inspectors to investigate what happened.

But photographs appeared to show the tracks had bent, possibly buckled.

Railway engineer Gareth Dennis told The Independent: “The damage here is as likely to be caused by the train as it derailed down the embankment, so very difficult to confirm a buckle with the available evidence.”

Residents of homes near the scene took chairs to a community hub for casualties to sit on.

One resident, Oriana Evans, who with her son helped casualties to the community centre at Lewes, said some of them seemed in shock and told her they were alright but “really bruised”.

open image in gallery Rail and emergency workers helped free people who had initially been trapped on board ( AFP/Getty )

“They were in the carriages that rolled over,” she said.

Some of the casualties were on holiday, Ms Evans said.

Transport secretary Heidi Alexander said she was deeply concerned and was “working quickly with the rail industry and local partners to assist passengers”.

Eastbourne MP Josh Babarinde, who said one constituent had suffered rib injuries, wrote on social media: “Once this immediate emergency is over, there are some serious questions that must be answered about how this happened, how this situation will be mitigated against from happening again, and how those on board will be compensated for what they have suffered.”

British Transport Police said it was believed that two patients suffered serious injuries and a further nine had less serious injuries.

“Patients have been assessed and treated at the scene, with some transported to local hospitals,” the force added.

South East Coast Ambulance Service said 18 people were taken to hospital and two people made their own way there.

It said passengers who did not need hospital treatment were being cared for at a local community centre.

“This remains a complex and ongoing multi-agency response,” a spokesperson said.

Most trains between Brighton, Lewes and Eastbourne or Seaford were cancelled.

Former Nickelodeon star Christy Knowings has died at 46.

Knowings was hospitalized after an asthma attack that reportedly left her with brain damage. She was placed on life support and died Tuesday, as TMZ first reported.

She joined All That in late 1997 along with Leon Frierson and Danny Tamberelli. They starred in a cast that included Saturday Night Live’s Kenan Thompson, Kel Mitchell, and Nickelodeon breakout star Amanda Bynes.

Knowings’ standout characters during her time on the sketch comedy show included news anchor Brenda Stone, whose lucky pen had been stolen, and Jessica, the valley girl in the iconic “Whateverrr!” sketch opposite Bynes.

Her other Nickelodeon appearances included the Rosie O’Donnell sketch comedy pilot And Now This! and the game show Figure It Out.

open image in gallery Christy Knowings has died aged 46 ( Instagram )

Knowings also appeared in three episodes of Sesame Street alongside her brother Chris Knowings, singing a duet about what it’s like to be a twin.

As a singer, she released her song “To the World” in 2020, calling it a “hauntingly gritty folk single” in a post shared on X.

In 2022, Knowings voiced her support for Bynes amid her fight to end her conservatorship.

“Awesome! I was able to push my schedule around, and I WILL be joining my fellow @AllThatOfficial cast member @leeboytv tomorrow! We will be there in support of our All That fam, @amandabynes as she takes this head on,” she wrote in a post on X.

Just weeks before her death, Knowings shared on Instagram that she was to be honored by Black Beat Magazine.

“Honored to be featured as a Special Guest during the Black Beat Magazine Relaunch & BET Weekend Celebration. Looking forward to celebrating culture, music, and entertainment. See you June 28!” she wrote in the caption.

open image in gallery Knowings became known for several sketch characters during her time on ‘All That’ ( Nickelodeon )

That post is now filled with condolences from fans.

“You made lasting memories for many of our childhoods. Appreciate the laughs when I was young. God bless your family,” one fan commented while another wrote, “R.I.P. Thank you for being apart of my childhood!!”

Others paid tribute on X, writing, “46 is far too young. Another reminder that some news just shouldn’t have to be real. Rest in peace, Christy Knowings.”

“This is insane. RIP Christy. Wayy too young. Praying for her twin Chris and their family,” another wrote.

Knowings’s former castmate Thompson paid tribute with his own post. Accompanying a photo of Knowings, he wrote on Instagram: “Man this one hit hard!!! Rest well Christy!!! Never could have imagined this day!! Sending so much love to her family!! She was a real one and one of the funniest people out here!!! Gonna miss you buddy!!! Show @christyknowings some love y’all!!!”

Knowings is the second former All That cast member to die this year after Kianna Underwood was killed in a hit-and-run in January.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio was hit with an embarrassing community note on X on Wednesday after writing that “American citizenship is not for sale.”

As the crowdsourced fact-check noted, the Trump administration has in fact launched a similar program: the Trump Gold Card, which offers green card-like U.S. residency “in record time” for individuals who contribute $1 million to the government.

Rubio’s message was meant to announce the State Department’s Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force, which he wrote will “review the activity of visa holders, dismantle illegal birth tourism networks, and put an end to this heinous abuse of our nation's laws.”

The task force has already revoked more than 600 visas, Rubio said.

The Trump administration has made cracking down on visa fraud and revoking visas for other reasons a major priority.

open image in gallery Secretary of State Marco Rubio was roasted online for posting that ‘American citizenship is not for sale,’ despite the Trump administration effectively selling residency for $1 million through its Gold Card program ( AFP/Getty )

This week, it announced the State Department revoked more than 175,000 visas from foreign nationals since the president took office.

That’s quadruple the pace of the final year of the Biden administration, an analysis by The Guardian found.

The majority of the revocations were “due to law enforcement encounters for a range of criminal activity, with assault, driving under the influence, theft, and drug crimes being the leading causes,” the State Department said in a fact sheet on Tuesday.

The announcement noted that officials revoked visas for offenses ranging from political speech to people seeking to be “birth tourists.”

The Gold Card program appears to be getting off to a less successful start.

In April, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said just one person had been approved for the card and paid their $1 million fee, though he added that “hundreds” more people were in a queue to get theirs.

open image in gallery Last year, the Trump administration announced the creation of the Gold Card program, though the government has admitted it has gotten off to a slow start ( Getty )

He previously claimed around 10,000 people had signed up for one of the cards in a pre-registration phase.

"I would expect over time that we'd ⁠sell, ​you know, thousands of these ​cards and raise, you know, billions, billions of dollars," Lutnick told Reuters in December.

The program has faced legal challenges. In February, a group of university professors sued over the offering, arguing it unfairly prioritizes the wealthy and ignores existing immigration law. The Trump administration says the extra fees as part of the Gold Card program do not guarantee shorter wait times.

Overall, the Trump administration has sought to limit the number of immigrants entering the U.S. and increase the number of those expelled from it.

It has revoked Temporary Protected Status from thousands of immigrants in the U.S., who had previously been barred from removal because their home countries, such as Haiti, were deemed excessively unsafe or unstable.

The president has also attempted to shut down the border to asylum-seekers and has paused most refugee resettlement, other than for white South Africans that the administration has baselessly claimed are facing genocide.

The administration has taken other steps, including launching a Justice Department effort to “prioritize and maximally pursue” denaturalization cases against American citizens and pushing to end birthright citizenship despite a recent Supreme Court ruling.

News.title: Groom accused of raping woman helping plan his wedding the night before the ceremony
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

A Nebraska groom is accused of raping a woman who was helping with preparations for his wedding — a day before he was getting married.

Tyler Weber, 33, was arrested last week on charges of first-degree sexual assault and first-degree false imprisonment after DNA results contradicted his claims that he did not assault the victim, WOWT reported.

He is accused of raping the woman, who was 19 and married, and gathered with a group of people at Weber’s home to prepare for his wedding in May, a day before the nuptials.

The group had been drinking, and the victim told Scotts Bluff County Sheriff’s deputies that Weber grabbed her hand and wrist when her husband wasn’t looking. However, at some point, the rest of the group — including her husband — left, leaving the victim and Weber alone at his home in Mitchell, a city of about 1,500 in western Nebraska.

The victim told investigators that she was feeling drunk and decided to borrow clothes and spend the night. She said that Weber followed her, grabbed her by the wrist and pinned her against the stairs before pulling her onto the couch, where he assaulted her, according to authorities.

open image in gallery Tyler Weber, of Nebraska, is accused of sexually assaulting a woman who was helping him prepare for his wedding — a day before he was getting married ( Scotts Bluff County Jail )

She told investigators that he pulled down her shorts and performed a sex act as she repeatedly told him “No!”

Weber reportedly stopped the assault several times to say that he shouldn’t be doing this since his wedding was the next day. The victim also told authorities that he discussed his desire to have a threesome with her and his soon-to-be wife, according to the report.

The victim said that she tried to text her husband to tell him “bad things were happening” but eventually fell asleep, the report noted. She later woke up around 5:30 a.m. when the bride-to-be came downstairs, saw Weber holding the victim and began to yell at her.

It was not immediately clear how Weber and the victim knew each other. The victim told investigators that Weber begged her “not to tell anyone what happened” as she left the home that morning.

Medical personnel performed a rape exam on the victim, collecting DNA samples. A warrant was later issued for Weber’s DNA and he consented to the test.

Initial results did not prove Weber’s innocence. However, a more thorough DNA test, known as a YSTR DNA test, matched his DNA, court records showed. The positive DNA match led to his arrest and charges.

Weber’s bond was set at $215,000. He is due back in court on Monday.

News.title: ‘More pain’ to come after economic slowdown
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. The economy grew at a slower pace in the second quarter of the year, official figures show, under pressure from the Iran war.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc between April and June, down from 0.6pc in the first three months of the year, according to the Office for National Statistics.

The figures underline the challenge that the conflict poses for Andy Burnham, who has pledged to deliver “growth in every postcode”.

The Prime Minister has already been warned that the economy will slow further next year if Donald Trump continues his war in the Middle East.

Treasury officials have predicted UK growth of just 0.3pc in 2027 if the Strait of Hormuz stays blocked for the rest of this year.

That is far lower than the 1.6pc predicted by the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) in March, based on assumptions made before the start of the war. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Iran war threatens to cripple growth, Treasury warns Burnham | Officials predict economic expansion of just 0.3pc in 2027 if Strait of Hormuz stays blocked

2) Britain facing £54bn bill for North Sea shutdown | Costs soar amid shortage of specialised ships needed to clear up abandoned oil rigs

3) Ban on zero-hours contracts to cost companies up to £3bn | Businesses face huge bill to offer workers guaranteed hours under Employment Rights Act

4) Nvidia’s AI push has echoes of Enron, says Big Short investor | Michael Burry claims chip giant is engaging in ‘circular’ financing

5) Shadow bank founder battles to stave off bankruptcy threat | Paresh Raja launches legal claim to prevent administrators from chasing him for repayment

What happened overnight

Asian shares were mostly higher, powered by gains for AI-related stocks including computer chips as regional markets tracked a rally on Wall Street.

Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 advanced 1.6pc to 68,601.21. In South Korea, the Kospi jumped 4pc, climbing to 6,844.65, as shares in Samsung Electronics surged 5.4pcc. Computer chipmaker SK Hynix jumped 7.1pc.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose 0.3pc to 3,967.28, while the Shanghai Composite index added 0.5pc to 3,967.65.

In Australia, the S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.4pc to 9,155.80.

Data from the US on Wednesday showed consumer prices had risen in line with analysts’ expectations in July.

Wall Street stocks were boosted on Wednesday by gains made by tech companies CoreWeave and Super Micro Computer, both of which closed up by more than 19pc.

The Nasdaq Composite ended the session up 0.5pc, with the S&P 500 up nearly 0.3pc. The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished the session marginally down.

Oil prices were little changed as investors weighed the deadlock in talks between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, was broadly flat at nearly $89 a barrel.

News.title: H5N1 sparks a very Australian epidemic
News.content:
H5N1 bird flu has reached Australia’s shores and is threatening to infect some of the country’s most unique wildlife.

Australasia is the last continent to be hit by the highly infectious avian influenza H5N1, a new strain of which has been circulating worldwide since 2020.

Since recording its first case in June, more than 200 wild seabirds in Australia have been infected, with fears that the highly infectious flu could quickly ‘jump’ to other species.

While H5N1 has infected animals from foxes to sea lions in other parts of the world in recent years, the epidemic now threatens some of Australia’s most iconic wildlife – many of which are found nowhere else on earth.

An Australian government assessment of more than 2,000 native species warned that nearly one in five faces a high risk from the deadly H5N1 bird flu, with hundreds of unique birds and mammals vulnerable to severe population reductions or even extinction.

Those animals include iconic species like the Tasmanian devils, quolls, and dingoes.

Other aquatic mammals, including the platypus, which is only found in Australia, are at risk of infection through contact with bird droppings in shared wetlands and coastal environments.

News.title: Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end
News.content:
Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

News.title: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG
News.content:
His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

News.title: Advice, cookbooks and emergency pot noodles: Your best gifts for university students
News.content:
When it comes to sending a child or grandchild off to university, it can be tempting to fill their room with every conceivable gadget.

So to help, we asked the Telegraph Recommended Community for their best gift recommendations and their suggestions ranged from desk lamps to cookery books and supermarket gift cards.

Here are the essentials worth buying.

Kitchen basics

From cupboard essentials to electrical appliances and cookbooks, most readers say they’d gift kitchen equipment.

Thinking back to his university days, reader TJ, 43, from London, says “the main essentials are around kitchen items and good long lasting food”.

“It’s nice to have some bits to cook for others as well and to make friends quickly,” he adds.

Susan, 54, from the West Midlands, agrees, recommending “basic cooking equipment” as a key staple and “distinctive cutlery, plates and cups that are easily identified”, which are particularly useful for shared accommodation.

“A box of store cupboard ingredients such as olive oil, soy, stock cubes and spices to use when cooking,” is also well-received, she says.

News.title: Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check
News.content:
Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

Team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

Sports.title: England legend Steven Gerrard, 46, handed biggest TV role yet ahead of new Premier League season
Sports.content:
STEVEN GERRARD has bagged himself a new gig just days before the start of the new Premier League season.

The Liverpool legend, 44, has been a bit-part pundit for TNT Sports in recent years.



And the Kop icon has expanded his role with the broadcaster, who are preparing to broadcast a whopping 700 MATCHES across several competitions next season.

Gerrard will be a “regular presence throughout the campaign”, giving his takes on the Premier League, Champions League and FA Cup matches aired by the broadcaster.



But he won’t just be sitting in the studio; he’ll also, on occasion, join Darren Fletcher, Sam Matterface, Mike Minay and Adam Summerton in the commentary booth.

Gerrard’s increased presence will further bolster TNT’s already all-star punditry team



Joe Cole, Ally McCoist , Karen Carney, Owen Hargreaves, Joleon Lescott, Fara Williams, Steve McManaman, Lucy Ward, Glenn Hoddle, Jen Beattie, Martin Keown, Anita Asante, Joel Ward and Robbie Savage will all be back on our screens for the broadcast’s prolonged footie extravaganza next season.

Scott Young, EVP, WBD Sports Europe, said: “With more than 700 live matches across domestic and European football, TNT Sports and HBO Max is an essential destination for football fans this season.

“The sheer volume of world-class football we bring together means there’s always a big match, an unmissable moment, a compelling story or a trophy on the line.

“From the referee’s first whistle in August to the biggest finals in May, we’re looking forward to taking football coverage to a whole new level.
