Sports.title: West Ham bans much mocked half-and-half scarves from stadium for new season as fans are warned they will be confiscated
Sports.content:
WEST Ham bosses have banned much mocked half-and-half scarves for good.

The divisive neckwear — bearing the names of both home and away teams — are sold outside grounds across the country and are popular with tourists.

But die-hard fans despise them, and they are sometimes outlawed for one-off games against rivals as displaying away colours at the home end poses safety risks.



The Hammers, newly relegated to the Championship, have posted warning signs at their City of ­London Stadium.



They state: “West Ham United would like to remind supporters that half-and-half scarves and any items displaying the colours or crests of both clubs are permanently banned inside London Stadium.

“This policy applies at all fixtures.

“Supporters arriving with half-and-half scarves purchased from unofficial sellers will be required to hand them over to security staff at the security checkpoints and these scarves will not be returned.

“Fans wishing to purchase a scarf for the game are encouraged to visit the official West Ham United Stadium Store where a full range of official merchandise is available ahead of kick-off.”

The rule was brought in for the Hammers’ 3-1 League Cup win over Portsmouth last weekend.

The move divided fans. West Ham nut John Hayes told The Sun: “The scarves are for the tourists who take away from the match atmosphere created by die-hard fans, who are often priced out of attending by the rubberneckers.

“Having a rival club’s crest on view in the home end sparks all sorts of problems.



“These scarves deserve going into the bin — with hydration breaks.”

But Arsenal fan Frank DuPont hit back: “Football is meant to be for everyone.

Tourists spend the most in the club shops, and picking up a half-and-half scarf from a street vendor is not going to damage the match experience for fussy season ticket holders.”

Previous West Ham games where the scarves have been banned include last season’s home match against Tottenham Hotspur.

Sports.title: Arsenal and Galatasaray hold stunning transfer talks as ‘Victor Osimhen’s name comes up’ with two Gunners stars
Sports.content:
ARSENAL face a fight to sign Victor Osimhen – if they decide to press ahead with a move for the Galatasaray striker.

The Gunners are currently in talks with the Turkish club as they look to offload Ethan Nwaneri and Gabriel Martinelli.



And Osimhen’s name is said to have come up in those discussions between the two clubs.

But it is understood that Galatasaray are determined to keep hold of their star striker and do not want to sell him.



The Turkish giants have already rejected an offer of £111million this summer from an unnamed club, believed to be Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal.

Arsenal would find it hard to soften that stance, although they can take heart from Newcastle initially being adamant Bruno Guimaraes would not be sold.



Osimhen is a player that the Gunners have looked at in the past, including when Edu was their sporting director.

The 27-year-old scored 22 goals in all competitions last season and helped Galatasaray win the Turkish top flight.

The Gunners are in the market for a marquee attacker this summer, but failed in their attempts to sign Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior.

The club are also looking to offload players, with Martinelli and Nwaneri offered to Galatasaray.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Turkish side have indicated they would pay around £38m for Martinelli, yet it is unclear if the Brazilian would be happy to move there.

Nwaneri, 19, is thought to prefer a move to Germany – if he leaves Arsenal – and is of interest to both Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig.

Dortmund have long admired the midfielder and were keen on him last summer, before he signed a five-year contract at the Emirates.

Arsenal hope to offload striker Gabriel Jesus and Napoli are currently the favorites to land the Brazilian.



Fabio Vieira hopes to return to Hamburg after spending last season on loan there, but a fee is proving hard to agree.

Reiss Nelson is a target for West Ham and the Hammers are hopeful of striking a deal, despite being in the Championship.

Sports.title: Arsenal files: Pre-season clash cancelled due to TYPHOON as famous referee retires on Emirates pitch
Sports.content:
ARSENAL fans will dominate the stands in this Sunday’s Community Shield against Manchester City.

The Gunners have been handed over 7,000 extra tickets to the curtain-raiser after Man City failed to sell out their full allocation at the Principality Stadium.



Arsenal were originally handed 25,218 tickets for the fixture, but are now expected to have close to 35,000 fans in Cardiff for the game.

A sea of red is expected in the stands, with Arsenal’s allocation stretching around almost 75 per cent of the seats available to supporters.



The game is being played in Wales due to a concert at Wembley Stadium this weekend, yet Arsenal’s players may feel like they are playing at the Emirates thanks to the enormous travelling support.

Fabregas’ sly return

Cesc Fabregas couldn’t wait to return to the Emirates Stadium on Wednesday night for Arsenal vs Como.



So much so that the former Gunners midfielder was in the stands for Arsenal’s pre-season defeat to Borussia Dortmund three days prior.

Fabregas’ Como side spent the week training in the UK and Fabregas made a point of coming to the Emirates to watch the Dortmund game before returning again on Wednesday.

It wasn’t the only time he has watched a game from the stands in recent years.

Fabregas was also present for Arsenal’s famous victory over Real Madrid in the Champions League two seasons ago.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The retired midfielder has an unusual relationship with Arsenal supporters given his move to Chelsea late in his career.

But the Emirates faithful ensured he was given a warm welcome during Wednesday night’s 1-1 draw with Como.

New backroom staff member

Arsenal have made further changes to their medical department by hiring Yeray Abreu Martinez.



The Spaniard is a strength and conditioning coach, who specialises in the rehab of players.

Most recently, he had been working with Saudi Arabian club Al Ittihad but he has now joined the Gunners.

In a statement on social media, Martinez said: “Proud and grateful to be part of the Arsenal family.

“A new chapter that I embrace with great commitment and ambition, looking forward to what’s ahead in this great project.”

Arsenal made sweeping changes to their medical team this summer and Martinez is one of several new faces.



Consultant Joaquin Acedo – who has known Arteta for decades – has played a key role in the revamp.

Teens’ typhoon trouble

Arsenal’s youngsters saw part of their pre-season preparations CANCELLED due to a typhoon.

The Gunners’ Under-17 side had been taking part in the Shanghai Future Stars Cup in China and made it to the final after a penalty shootout win over Shanghai U17s.

Arsenal were due to face China’s U17s in the final, but the match was scrapped due to dangerous weather conditions.



The Young Guns were named joint-winners of the tournament after the game was scuppered by the typhoon.

Highly-rated teenager Jaden Maghoma won the golden boot after netting four times during the tournament.

Arsenal’s travelling squad also included rising star Luis Munoz, Ethan Nwaneri’s brother Emerson Nwaneri, and Mikel Arteta’s son Gabriel Arteta.

Tzol the rage

Christos Tzolis made his debut in the Premier League five years ago against…Arsenal.



Tzolis and his Norwich team suffered a 1-0 loss at the Emirates on September 11, 2021.

Had the Canaries won, manager Mikel Arteta would have been under massive pressure as it would have been a fourth successive top-flight loss for the Spaniard.

Arsenal scored with a scrappy 66th-minute winner from Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, with the visitors believing that VAR missed a handball and Tzolis, a £9million arrival from PAOK, was replaced a couple of minutes later by Daniel Farke.

Norwich’s former sporting director Stuart Webber recalled: “Christos scored twice against Bournemouth in the League Cup so he started at Arsenal.

“We’d lost the first three games of the season. We’d lost against Liverpool at home, Manchester City away, Leicester at home.



“But they’d also lost the first three games of the season.

“Arteta, in that game, was under huge pressure. You’d have to ask them, but I’m pretty sure if we’d rocked up and beat them, it would’ve been a problem.

“I remember Nicolas Pepe was playing for them. Brandon Williams had him in his pocket. It was the scrappiest 1-0 game. Let’s say their goal ricocheted off a handball.

“A fair result would’ve been his draw, but yes, Christos made his debut in the Premier League that day.”



Five years later, Tzolis will be looking to make his Premier League debut for Arsenal against Coventry next Friday.

Webber added: “I’m delighted he’s gone and done what he’s done. He’s just a really good guy who cares a lot. I think it hurt him that it didn’t quite work out with us.”

Ref’s farewell

Assistant referee Sian Massey-Ellis ended her officiating career at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday.

The lineswoman announced last week that she would be hanging up her flag and had a final send-off in North London for Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup.

Her final match was celebrated behind the scenes at the stadium before she had one last outing ahead of a move to an FA position.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Massey-Ellis has officiated in over 150 Premier League matches since making her debut in 2010.

She is set to become The FA‘s Senior Manager for Women Referees from September, where she will support and develop female officials across the country.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo shows off dramatic new look days after marrying Georgina Rodriguez
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO RONALDO has reported back for Al-Nassr duties sporting a dramatic new look.

The five-time Ballon d’Or winner has enjoyed some rest and relaxation since Portugal were dumped out of the World Cup by Spain on July 6.



He has also tied the knot with long-term partner Georgina Rodriguez – the pair announcing their marriage in a joint Instagram post earlier this week.

And it seems CR7 has been celebrating his new chapter by getting busy with the hair dye.



Ronaldo posted a picture to his Instagram story on Thursday which featured yellow and blue circle emojis – the colours of Al-Nassr.

He also wore a short-sleeve black t-shirt, a necklace, a glitzy watch and carried a Gucci wash bag.

Nothing out of the ordinary there, then.

But on top of Ronaldo’s head was a gelled crop of dyed hair.

The Portuguese, 41, has gone from his usual dark brown to an eye-catching gold.

It does not quite match his dark eyebrows but Ronaldo will certainly stand out on the pitch as he chases down 1,000 career goals this season.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Fans went wild on social media, with one X user commenting: “Married Ronaldo already looking different.”

Another added: “Looking fresh my GOAT.”

A third joked: “Inspired by his idol Garnacho.”

And a fourth chimed in with: “Eminem 2.0.”

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola copycats have been ruining the EFL slams veteran boss Tony Mowbray
Sports.content:
PEP GUARDIOLA copycats have been ruining EFL football.

That is the damning verdict from veteran boss Tony Mowbray as Blackburn travel to Wolves tonight for the Championship curtain-raiser.



And Mowbray, 62, insists a generation of bosses have been brainwashed into over-complicating the game with total-football tactics their players cannot pull off.

The Rovers boss told SunSport: “Pep Guardiola changed the landscape of football.



“People say it almost spoilt the game because everybody wants to play like Pep — but we can’t all play like him.

“In 2012, he had a formidable team at Barcelona with Xavi and Iniesta, a generation full of talent playing a false nine.



“A generation of coaches have come through inspired by him, inverting full-backs and playing overloads in different areas.

“And yet every week in lower leagues we see teams giving pathetic goals away by the goalie trying to play a little triangle in his box.

“At teams lower down, it’s much more difficult. It’s easier to press than to be the team with the ball.

“We can’t all play like Pep — you need a fusion of football and pragmatism.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Mowbray believes the era of blind possession copycats is finally shifting into a far more practical, diverse age of football.

Mowbray said: “I think it’s riveting. Guardiola’s left now, and I think the game will resort back — not back to the 80s where everybody just has a striker and a little guy fast over the top.

“But I think it will become more diverse. More teams will be playing off the front and beating the press.

“It will become more pragmatic as well. I think there’s going to be a really special, good era of football.

“I love the game, all aspects of it. I can see the benefits of having a big centre-forward who can bring it in or flick it on, playing over the top of all these pressing teams who understand where the pressing lines are.



“When teams commit so many men to a press to win the ball high up, if you play over it, you’re two passes away and you can score. I think that’s really thought-provoking.

“That’s why I love the job of being a coach — analysing the teams we’re going to play and seeing whether we are going to kick every goal kick long today, or build from the back with four or five men and play through their lines. I like the idea of a team who can do both. A fusion of football.”

That obsession with trendy coaching metrics and extra tactical staff almost made Mowbray fall out of love with the game.

In early 2024, his world was turned upside down when forced to step down from Birmingham following a bowel cancer diagnosis.

And after undergoing surgery and treatment, Mowbray admits modern football’s push toward technical directors interfering with squad selection made him question returning.



He said: “I started thinking I wasn’t enjoying where football was going.

“I remember once trying to sign a very young Gerard Pique for Hibs on loan from Manchester United.

“I was at a petrol station, looked at my phone that was ringing and it said Alex Ferguson. I didn’t know whether to keep filling my car or take the call.

“I stopped and answered. He couldn’t let me have Pique but told me, ‘I’d advise you to have total control. The only way to succeed is to have control so players know who the boss is.’



“When I was at West Brom against Sir Alex, he’d come in for a drink and talk about control. That’s gone now.

“There are too many layers. Do I want to get told by a technical director who to pick or why players ran too hard? It’s about trust.”

That search for respect drew Mowbray back to Ewood Park following his recovery.

Following a short interim spell at West Brom last season, a homecoming at Blackburn gave him what Sir Alex insisted on… freedom to manage.

Mowbray said: “The job has become harder for coaches. I’ve always felt the manager needs to manage and pick the team.



“I found integrity and honesty in this ownership model. They look me in the eye and let me get on with it. The respect is there.

“There are different layers from when I was here before, but I don’t want total control. I want to do it together.”

Mowbray points to Blackburn’s academy products as proof that passing quality and direct power must coexist.



Crystal Palace and England midfielder Adam Wharton came through the ranks during Mowbray’s last spell between 2017 and 2022.

He said: “Adam was only 14 or 15 — but he’d train with the first team because he was so special with the ball.

“Jon Dahl Tomasson, who followed me, gave him his debut and Adam allowed the team to play an amazing passing game.

“I love seeing that, but I see the benefits of a big centre-forward who can bring it in or flick it on, playing over pressing teams.

“It’s a fusion of football. You have to figure it out.”



Despite his wariness of all the layers of analysts and technical staff in football, do not brand Mowbray a dinosaur.

He said: “I like data pointing us to the right players.

“There might be a winger in Belgium’s second division putting in the most crosses and I’d never know until data points at him.

“Then your wisdom correlates whether he can step up to Championship level and if he has the right personality to fit your group. Ultimately, data cannot tell you that.”

Mowbray admits his time off while fighting illness left him climbing the walls at home.



And with his children flying the nest for university, the family hit a major turning point.

Mowbray revealed: “I was driving everyone mad at home! Walking the dog was the highlight of my day.

“My kids are older now. One is 19 and flying off to college in America. We’re at a crossroads as a family because everyone’s flying the nest.



“How relieved is my wife Amber that I got back to work? She’s happy. She knows football is my driving force.

“She’s made so many sacrifices and deserves a medal.”

Back at Ewood Park, the thrill of managing still burns.

Mowbray said: “Seven months at home with the health pressure, I had dark moods.

“People asked if I looked at retirement — but my fire still burns. Why do I love it? Because you’re dealing with 30 individuals every day.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Some feel they’re the best player in town, asking, ‘Why am I not playing?’ Others are quiet and shy, yet they’re the best technicians, and you try to bring personality out of them.

“It’s an amazing job. You need trust and empathy. Computers are great, but you need a human touch.”

Sports.title: Wilfried Zaha training at Premier League club six weeks after becoming unemployed
Sports.content:
WILFRIED ZAHA has been using Crystal Palace’s training ground to stay sharp this summer.

The winger, 33, scored 90 goals in 458 appearances across two spells with the Eagles – the second of which ended in 2023.



And excitement has been growing among Palace fans around Zaha potentially returning for a third stint.

But SunSport understands that Zaha’s sessions at Copers Cope Road are only part of an informal arrangement.



Palace agreed to grant Zaha personal use of the facilities until he finds a new club.

And a longer-term deal that could see the former Manchester United star lace up for Palace again is not under consideration.



Zaha posted a video montage showing him dribbling past training dummies and firing into netted goals on Thursday.

The comments section was chock-full of Palace fans trying to persuade him to come back.

But the decision rests with the club, who have already signed winger Dwight McNeil this summer and are weighing up a swoop for Solly March.

Zaha has been a free agent since his Galatasaray contract expired at the end of June.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Ivory Coast international scored 10 goals in 43 games for the Turkish side but was shipped out on loan twice during his time there.

His loan at Lyon was cut short halfway through the season after six goalless appearances.

And the French club’s manager at the time, Pierre Sage, is now in charge of Palace.

Zaha then spent a year and a half on loan at Charlotte, scoring 13 goals in 48 games.

Sports.content:

Antoine Semenyo’s brilliant backheel saw the Manchester outfit fend off Chelsea in a tense Wembley final.

Now England’s top two go head-to-head for the chance to pick up the first bit of silverware this season, and tickets are flying off the shelf.

Sports.title: McIlroy makes woeful start to FedExCup Playoffs as Spieth shares early lead
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy made a woeful start to the FedExCup Playoffs as he shot four-over par opening round at the FedEx St. Jude Championship in Memphis.

Playing for the first time since finishing tied for 40th at The Open at Royal Birkdale almost a full month ago, McIlroy was level par going into the final three holes before a disastrous streak left him towards the rear of the field.

Dropped shots at 16 and 17 were followed by a double bogey at TPC Southwind's final hole, which came after McIlroy found the water with his tee shot to the closing par four.

The 74 left McIlroy nine shots adrift of the early leaders, with American duo Jordan Spieth and Michael Thorbjornsen setting the early pace with 65s.

England's Tommy Fleetwood, who was paired with Spieth, was a shot off that mark after opening up with a 66 that included a delightful chip in for eagle at the par-five third hole.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tommy Fleetwood produced this eagle on third hole at the FedEx St. Jude Championship.

Fleetwood said: "I feel good. I didn't really play very good in the practice days. Game's not really been that great. I've been showing a lot, like some good and some really not so good.

"Hit it great off the tee today. Still my iron play was iffy, but I did a good job of managing it for the most part. Still hit some really good shots, and you can never underestimate how good - I think shooting under par on this golf course is very good."

World No 1 Scottie Scheffler, who played alongside McIlroy in the marquee group for the opening two rounds, put himself in a solid position by delivering a 68.

Scheffler said: "I felt like I hit a lot of quality shots with my irons.I did a good job of being patient and not trying to force it too much.

"I feel like I was right on the edge of having a good day, kind of all day is how I would describe it. So, I felt like patience-wise, I did a pretty good job."

Fleetwood had European company towards the top of the leaderboard, with Ludvig Aberg and Sepp Straka both joining Scheffler on two-under.

McIlroy could at least take consolation from not having the worst round of the day, which belonged to Scotland's Robert MacIntyre, who shot a 12-over par 82.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Sky Sports Golf Podcast, Jamie Weir and Brad Faxon debate whether Rory McIlroy's extended break since The Open will help him win a record-extending fourth FedExCup title.

Memphis is hosting the first of three FedExCup Playoffs events, with only the top 50 in the overall season standings at the end of Sunday's final round progressing to the BMW Championship, and then the top 30 qualifying for the season-ending Tour Championship.

McIlroy's position of 12th out of the 70-player field means there is no concern about his progress to the BMW Championship, while the fact the events have no cut gives him plenty of time to climb the leaderboard over the weekend.

How do the FedExCup Playoffs work?

All season long, players have earned points based on how they have performed in PGA Tour events, with extra points available for the signature events and majors.

Only the top 70 in the standings have reached the FedEx St Jude Championship (August 13-16), with just the top 50 then progressing to the BMW Championship (August 20-23) and then only the top 30 making it to the finale, The Tour Championship (August 27-30).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brooks Koepka was extremely disappointed after failing to make the FedExCup playoffs.

Winners of the first two play-off events earn 750 points apiece - the same as The Players and the majors - before the points reset to zero ahead of the Tour Championship.

In the closing event, all players begin at even par, with the starting-strokes model based on FedExCup placings at that point axed in 2025.

The winner of the Tour Championship becomes FedExCup champion for 2026, earning $10m (£7.4m) and a five-year PGA Tour exemption.

Live coverage of the first event of the PGA Tour's FedExCup Playoffs, the FedEx St. Jude Championship, continues at 5pm on Friday. Watch live on Sky Sports Golf and Sky Sports Main Event or stream with no contract.

Sports.title: Leicester City up for sale for more than £200m
Sports.content:
Thai owners King Power are seeking to sell Leicester City for more than £200m.

The former Premier League champions engaged with Citibank to sound out potential buyers, it was reported last month.

Sky Sports News has now seen a sales pitch brochure produced by the investment bank, detailing the investment opportunity and the infrastructure which is included for sale at the club.

The dossier lists as up for sale: the men's and women's teams, King Power Stadium, both the women's and the men's training facilities, and OH Leuven, Leicester's sister club in Belgium.

The project is titled "Project Lineup" and values the physical assets at £224m with no specific sum placed on the sale of King Power's football teams.

In 2023, the club purchased the land around the King Power stadium for redevelopment, with plans to expand the capacity to 40,000, build a new hotel and entertainment complex.

Citigroup forecast the club's revenue during the 2026 financial year to be £97m.

However, the bank do not mention the club's two relegations between 2023 and 2025 and the financial losses that caused.

Image: Leicester City won the Premier League 10 years ago but are now in League One

King Power, run by the Srivaddhanaprabha family, bought Leicester for £35m from Milan Mandaric in 2010.

In recent years, King Power have converted a lot of debt into equity, to the tune of almost £300m. That has meant, apart from some small maintenance loans, the club is largely debt-free.

Sky Sports News has been told King Power have no urgency to sell, and they will continue to fund the club to the fullest until such time as a new, credible buyer steps forward. They have backed head coach Russell Martin this summer, with nine new signings.

The document states that Leicester is the sixth most successful team in English football since 2000, making this a "rare opportunity" to buy a club with a record of "winning promotions to higher divisions".

Image: Leicester City famously won the Premier League in 2015/16

As well as their surprise Premier League win in 2016, Leicester also won the FA Cup and Community Shield in 2021.

These successes are all included in the sales pitch, but their current position in League One is not referenced.

The document also cites Ben Chilwell, Harvey Barnes and Kieran Dewsbury-Hall as profitable recent transfers, with Gary Lineker and Emile Heskey listed at notable former players.

Sky Sports News contacted Leicester City for comment but they have declined to do so.

Analysis: 'Finding the right purchaser could take years'

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett:

"On the face of it, it seems bizarre that King Power would look to sell Leicester City at a time when the club is at its lowest ebb, and at one of its lowest market values, with the team in League One after three relegations in four seasons.

"But in truth Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha has been seeking new investment for several years - all that is new here is the glossy brochure which advertises the club for sale, accentuating its assets. It is now being actively marketed for sale by financial specialists.

Image: Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha holding the FA Cup

"That brochure - unusual as it is - is concrete evidence of a looming end of an era. King Power want out - having delivered unprecedented success in the form of the most unlikely of Premier League titles, an FA Cup, Champions League football and a Community Shield.

"For some Leicester fans, all that success has been tarnished by recent failures, and there have been protests against the ownership, and the director of football, Jon Rudkin. Serious mistakes have been made, for sure, in the management of the club in recent years, which has seen Leicester crash into League One, after boasting to be the club which came closest to breaking the "Big Six" Premier League monopoly over the last decade.

"But those dissenting Leicester fans should be careful what they wish for. On the open market, the football club is a very attractive prospect - almost entirely debt-free (thanks to the generosity of King Power in turning almost all of their £300m debt into equity in recent years) and with fully owned assets that are the envy of much bigger clubs in the Premier League. Their Seagrave training ground is a better facility than all but a handful of others in Europe.

"However, despite all their recent success, Leicester's fan-base is not as sizeable as many of the big clubs in the Championship, and having dropped into the third tier, even promotion at the first attempt would mean they didn't have the benefit of parachute payments in the second tier. All of those facts will be taken into account by would-be buyers.

"So don't expect a quick sale of the club. It could take years to find the right purchaser. The good news for Foxes fans is that King Power will not relinquish their responsibility as custodians, just because they have made the decision to sell. Nine new signings this summer is evidence of their determination to still support the football club. And the goodwill that the Thai business leaders still have for Leicester will almost certainly mean that they won't sell to the highest bidder, just to make a quick buck.

"Khun "Top" knows his legacy is at stake, and in memory of his late father, who died tragically in a helicopter crash in the stadium car park, he will no doubt want to sell the club to a new owner who can take the club forward, and once again make it a success."

Sports.title: Draper beaten in Cincinnati first round after blowing second-set lead
Sports.content:
Jack Draper lost 6-3 7-5 to Martin Landaluce in the first round of the Cincinnati Open after blowing six set-point chances to level the match.

Little more than a week on from a first-round defeat in Montreal on his return from injury, Draper was once more unable to maintain a consistent level as he succumbed to the Spaniard.

After being broken in the first game of the match on his way to losing the first set, Draper looked set to level when he went 5-2 up in the second having secured a double-break.

However, he would fail to take six set points spread across the next three games as Landaluce broke twice to level at 5-5.

Draper saved a match point for Landaluce before bringing up a chance of his own to force a tie break, but he was denied before his opponent closed out the match in just short of two hours.

The 24-year-old appeared extremely glum in the closing stages, but at least appeared to finish the match without any major fitness issues.

During his defeat to Terence Atmane in Montreal, the power of Draper's shots notably dropped off in the third set, while he was also in tears during the changeover.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack Draper in tears on return from injury at the Canadian Open.

The circumstances in Montreal suggested Draper had reaggravated the left-arm injury that has plagued him since June 2025, at which point he had reached a career-high world ranking of fourth, but a swift return to the practice courts in Cincinnati calmed concern over his physical state.

While only Draper and his team know his true physical condition, it is clear that he is struggling to find anything like his best form, with the final major of the year - the US Open - starting in New York on August 30.

Sports.title: Doyle: Coppull can strike in the Hungerford
Sports.content:
Our ambassador previews four contests on Newbury's Hungerford Day and assesses the big races at Ripon - both cards live on Sky Sports Racing.

Extra furlong ideal for Hungerford fancy

Coppull showed me enough in the Group One July Cup to convince me he is up to taking the Visit Malta Hungerford Stakes (3.10) at Newbury on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Racing.

Clive Cox's three-year-old took a long time to get organised at Newmarket where the winner - Comanche Brave - got first run but this strong traveller should enjoy the extra furlong on a more conventional track.

Never So Brave will have his supporters on the back of his second in the Criterion at York over this seven-furlong trip but is struggling to get his head in front this season while Godolphin's Symbol Of Honour is solid but has never won over this distance.

A more interesting runner for me is William Haggas's Extremely Zain, a course and distance winner who ran better than his final placing suggests in the International at Ascot and remains on an upward curve. This is a step up in grade, but he can acquit himself well in an ordinary renewal.

Millionaire sets standard in Geoffrey Freer

Dubai Honour, who has four Group Ones and over £5 million in prize money on his CV, can roll back the years in the opening Highclere Thoroughbred Racing Geoffrey Freer Stakes (1.25) at Newbury.

This eight-year-old has given my husband Tom (Marquand) some of his finest moments in the saddle and, with an excellent record fresh, can make it win number 11 on his return from a summer break.

There is little between Mount Atlas and Tabletalk on their efforts in the Silver Cup at York, but I can't see either finding the improvement needed to lower the colours of Dubai Honour on these terms.

Gamrai went down fighting in the Copper Horse at Royal Ascot and, whilst he's in deeper waters now, may just benefit from the change of scenery, having joined George Scott from John and Thady Gosden.

Fire can burn it up in Sprint Handicap

Now he has got his head back in front, Richard Hannon's Wheels Of Fire can put up another bold show in the D&H, Excellence In Nutrition Handicap (1.55) at Newbury.

He beat the re-opposing Hypnotised comfortably at Sandown and a six-pound rise may not be enough to stop him following up under Pat Dobbs, even though that rival is better off at the weights.

Chris Mason's Glamorous Breeze is entitled to go close on her solid performance at Goodwood, but Kinswoman has come up short in Listed and Group company and still has something to prove, even though she's dropping back into a handicap off a reduced rating.

Humam set to build on Newmarket third

Humam's front-running third in a warm race at Newmarket puts him bang there for the TPT Fire Handicap (2.35) at Newbury. I loved the way this former Andrew Balding runner stuck to the task to register his best effort for Stuart Williams since being gelded in the winter.

Racing off an unchanged mark, his most recent form is more compelling than that of market rival Scoville, who has disappointed in both the Royal Hunt Cup and the Golden Mile at Goodwood and needs to improve for this drop in trip.

Eve Johnson Houghton's admirable Great Acclaim has been running well in big races such as the Victoria Cup and Buckingham Palace but needs some respite from the handicapper.

Roxby can initiate big-race double

Malton trainer Nigel Tinkler and his apprentice Alex Jary have a great chance of pulling off a memorable big race double at Ripon on Saturday, starting with Lord Roxby in the William Hill/MND Association Great St Wilfrid Handicap (3.25).

Middleham Park's four-year-old returns to the North Yorkshire track in top form after beating fancied rival Dark Cloud Rising over course and distance at the start of the month. He also put a big field to the sword at York earlier this summer and can cope with a five-pound rise against some smart rivals who have a bit more to prove.

Likely favourite Fast Track Harry put in an improved performance in first-time cheekpieces at Ascot last time but I'm not convinced the track will suit while the class horse in the race, Aramram, must overcome a low draw and he ran badly from a similar position in this race two years ago.

Boy can turn on the Magic in Silver Cup

In the consolation race, the William Hill Supporting MND Silver Cup Handicap (2.55), Nigel runs Magic Boy who ticks plenty of boxes in a wide open, big field dash.

This four-year-old is less exposed than most and showed his potential with a hard-fought win against 18 rivals at York last month before a slow start compromised his chances back there three weeks ago.

Magic Boy is ideally drawn in stall 14 and has previous track form which is always so important at the Garden Racecourse. He has finished second on both his visits but can go one better despite needing a career best.

Another interesting contender is Clive Cox's Mythical Composer who is also potentially well-drawn in stall 15 but needs to bounce back from a poor effort at Goodwood, his first since being gelded.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

Sports.title: Celtic sign midfielder Baur on an initial four-year deal
Sports.content:
Celtic have made their fourth summer signing with midfielder Mika Baur joining on an initial four-year deal, with the option for a further year.

The 22-year-old arrives in a deal worth around £6.8m, joining from German club Paderborn, after helping them win promotion from the second tier of German football to the Bundesliga.

He scored four times and provided five assists across 33 league appearances last season, and was named the club's player of the year.

Sky Sports News understand the Scottish champions will pay an initial fee of around £4.5m for Baur, with £2.3m in add-ons making up the deal.

Similar to deals struck with fellow summer signings Camilo Duran, Kasper Høgh and Haissem Hassan, a large proportion of the bonuses will be paid out if Celtic reach the league phase of the Champions League.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Summer signing Kasper Hogh scored a hat-trick in just his second league game at Celtic

Celtic face LASK Linz in their play-off tie next week, and Baur - who came through the youth ranks at Freiburg before moving to Paderborn in 2024 - could now be registered for that Champions League squad.

On joining the Scottish Champions, Baur said: "It's absolutely the right move.

"It's a great club and I've heard incredible things about the fans.

"I'm in the same agency as Nicolas Kuhn so I called him to ask a couple of questions and he was so positive. He said, if you have the chance, just do it.

"I've had a good pre-season with good matches and tough training sessions, everything. So I'm in good shape and I'm ready to go."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Simeon Gholam explains all you need to know on how the play-offs have changed this season in the Championship

Wolves v Blackburn, Friday 8pm, live on Sky Sports

Image: Wolves vs Blackburn

Wolves hold the tag of second favourites for the Championship title at 5/1 with Sky Bet - and rightly so - but I'm always wary of backing teams that have made losing football matches a habit, especially in the early stages of a season when playing a level down.

When assessing the last 10 teams that enter the Championship having taken 25 or points or less in the Premier League, their record across the first five games of the season is poor. Of those 50 games, the relegated team won just 15 - a strike rate of just 30 per cent.

The market has Wolves in at 1/2 here, meaning an implied probability of 66 per cent. That looks a shade too high for me, based on the unknowns still regarding this Wolves side. Also, those 50 games also produced a goals per game average of 2.1 which points towards this being a low-scoring fiddly opener for Wolves, who might be lacking some rhythm.

Tony Mowbray takes charge of Blackburn again and despite his health issues and below-par results at his last three clubs, his teams did only concede 1.1 expected goals per 90 minutes across that 85-game sample size. Under 2.5 goals at Evens with Sky Bet is the bet.

SCORE PREDICTION: 1-1 | JONES KNOWS' BEST BET: Under 2.5 goals (Evens with Sky Bet)

Bolton v Preston, Saturday 12.30pm, live on Sky Sports

Image: Bolton vs Preston

Preston had a very strong record away from home against the bottom half last season, losing just three of those 15 games but there was a big over-performance which averaged at 0.9 goals per game when you analyse the expected goals supremacy.

The departure of captain Ben Whiteman to Wrexham and the loss of important attacking contributions from Lewis Dobbin and Daniel Jebbison also give Paul Heckingbottom a problem. He saw his team lose four on the bounce in pre-season and a season of struggle could be on the cards.

Looking at previous seasons, newly-promoted teams in the Championship have a solid record of starting the season full of momentum and Bolton can land favourites backers a winner here at 5/4 with Sky Bet.

SCORE PREDICTION: 2-1

Bristol City v Millwall, Saturday 3pm, live on Sky Sports

There is a temptation to look at Millwall's third-place finish last season and think: that was a bit of a freak, wasn't it?

I don't think it was.

Millwall were third because they were really good at accumulating points.

They won 24 of their 46 league matches, lost only 11 and conceded just 49 goals. Alex Neil has brought a greater degree of tactical flexibility without taking away the characteristics you associate with Millwall. His teams are organised, competitive and pragmatic but there is more individual quality within this squad than we've seen from many previous Millwall sides.

This summer represents a more substantial attempt to change direction for Bristol City which makes them a difficult team to rate, but with such upheaval this looks a good time for Millwall to go there and do Millwall things. Away win at 17/10 with Sky Bet.

SCORE PREDICTION: 1-2

Middlesbrough v Lincoln, Saturday 3pm, live on Sky Sports

If you were judging teams on how well they actually played football rather than simply counting the goals that went in, there is a very strong argument that Middlesbrough were the best team in the Championship once Kim Hellberg took charge.

The underlying numbers were exceptional. Boro allowed fewer shots than anyone in the division and produced the Championship's best shot ratio. They collected 80 points from an expected 83.2 and created 109 big chances while conceding only 68. Few teams have a stronger statistical case for improvement.

Hellberg has had his first full pre-season to refine a side that increasingly carries his identity: aggressive, possession-heavy and designed to overwhelm opponents territorially.

Hayden Hackney has left but Hellberg has the credentials to plug that gap. They look a great bet to win promotion at 5/2 with Sky Bet and can start with a home win.

Norwich v West Brom, Saturday 3pm, live on Sky Sports

Norwich averaged only 0.91 points per game across their opening 23 fixtures but 1.91 across the final 23.

Richards (20-4-1, 13 KOs) is a world-ranked former British champion who fought Dmitry Bivol for the WBA light-heavyweight title in 2021. He won his two most recent fights in 2025, including a knockout win over Dan Azeez last December.

The fight will mark the first time hard-hitting, Serbian-born Kalajdzic (30-3, 22 KOs) has fought outside North America as a professional. The 35-year-old's last fight was a seventh-round knockout victory against Oleksandr Gvozdyk in February.

The Copper Box Arena bill will also feature a 10-round middleweight showdown between British boxers Cutler and Greene.

Cutler beat Stevie McKenna on points when they fought in December 2024, marking the only professional defeat for Ireland's KO king so far.

Image: Lee Cutler and Louis Greene clash at middleweight

Cutler's last fight saw him stop Aaron Sutton in his hometown of Bournemouth in three rounds, while Greene - a former Commonwealth super-welterweight champion - earned a points decision win over Daniel Buciuc in Dublin last week.

Decorated British amateur Kayla Allen is also fighting as part of her professional debut after becoming the first female fighter to sign with Zuffa Boxing.

Alex MacMillan, Leon Hughes and Fred Pullen, who is also turning professional, are also on the London bill.

Richards: My story isn't written yet - the time is now

Craig "Spider" Richards speaking on Sky Sports News:

"It's a very exciting fight. Everyone knows Kalajdzic can punch, I can punch, we've both been two fighters who haven't shied away from competition.

"We've been in with everyone, we've mixed it, we both probably want to push on now towards that world title and I feel like it's a great opportunity.

"UK vs USA - that mix always goes down well! I'm up for it, I'm excited and I think this is now going to be the best version of me going into the new chapter and I get to go and display what I'm about.

Image: Richards is looking for another shot at a world title

"I feel like my story is not written yet and I feel like I need to write it now.

"The problem we had before is that a lot of opponents were turning [a fight with] me down, saying 'he's a hard fight, he's a long night in the office'.
