Sports.title: Jamie O’Hara: Wrexham would walk the Scottish Premiership, Celtic and Rangers are Championship level
Sports.content:
Jamie O’Hara: Wrexham would walk the Scottish Premiership, Celtic and Rangers are Championship level

Celtic and Rangers can disregard competing in the Premier League - they're not good enough for the English top flight.

That's according to Jamie O'Hara who, in comparison, believes that Wrexham would storm their way to the Scottish Premiership title.

3 Celtic are Scottish champions, but O'Hara thinks Wrexham could conquer them Credit: Getty

Scottish football has long been dominated by Glaswegian rivals Celtic and Rangers given they've won a combined 111 league titles.

Both clubs have also been successful in Europe, especially Celtic, who became the first British team to win the European Cup in 1967.

Their statuses as Scottish juggernauts has led to many fans question whether or not they could stand firm in arguably the best league in world football - the Premier League.

However, ex-Tottenham Hotspur midfielder O'Hara has shut down any hope of them doing so by saying they're Championship quality at best.

"They'd get relegated out of the Premier League, if they were in the Premier League now," he declared on talkSPORT Drive.

Darren Bent agreed, before adding: "But if you put them in the Prem and gave them the finances that Premier League clubs...

"They'd be able to spend money because they've got huge fan bases all over the world."

Bent then asked what division Celtic and Rangers would suit, to which O'Hara replied: "Championship, League One. I wouldn't put them in League Two because they're better than that... maybe the Championship."

"You take those two teams out of Scottish football, and it's ruined," Bent added: "I wouldn't mind a year watching them in the FA Cup, though, just to see (how well they would do).

But O'Hara insisted that Wrexham would knock both out of the competition, which led to an interesting question from his co-host.

3 O'Hara doesn't think Celtic or Rangers are good enough for the Premier League Credit: Getty

O'Hara: Wrexham would 'walk' the Scottish Premiership

"Do you think Wrexham would go up to the Scottish league and win it?" Bent asked.

"Oh absolutely, absolutely. Yeah, they'd walk it," O'Hara confirmed. "Wrexham would walk Scottish football, they would."

O'Hara then explained how a gulf in finances would play a major role in Celtic and Rangers being unable to be the Premier League's best.

For example, Liverpool completed the most expensive signing in Premier League history last summer when Alexander Isak joined from Newcastle United for £125million.

On the other hand, the Scottish Premiership's equivalent is just £12m, which is when Rangers bought Tore Andre Flo from Chelsea in 2000.

"And that's not disrespect," O'Hara added. "They just would because the money's not there for them to be able to (compete)...

3 Wrexham have been backed by O'Hara to win the Scottish title if they were eligible Credit: Getty

"Celtic and Rangers, if you gave them four or five seasons playing in the English league, they'd become giants."

Bent disagreed, but O'Hara stuck to his word and backs Wrexham to hypothetically win the Scottish Premiership.

The Red Dragons are one of the favourites to earn promotion to the Premier League from the Championship in the 2026/27 campaign.

Wrexham came narrowly close to reaching the top tier last season, but finished seventh and two points outside the play-offs.

However, they could be set to benefit from a new format that makes its debut in the Championship this season.

The teams that finish from third to eighth will enter the play-offs, so six teams will compete instead of four.

Sports.title: Everton Women’s new goalkeeper has awkward tattoo and survived car crash despite broken neck
Sports.content:
Everton Women’s new goalkeeper has awkward tattoo and survived car crash despite broken neck

Everton Women's new signing, Rylee Foster-Inman, sports a Liverpool-inspired tattoo, having been a lifelong supporter of the Reds.

The Toffees announced the return of the Canadian goalkeeper on Wednesday, following her previous short stint with the Blues in 2024.



5 The keeper has strong family ties to the city Credit: Getty

The 27-year-old signed from Halifax Tides, having previously developed through the ranks at West Virginia Mountaineers before joining Liverpool in January 2020.

Now back on the blue side of the city, the shot-stopper expressed her excitement at the prospect of playing in front of the Goodison Park crowd.

However, Foster-Inman possesses a strong connection to the city of Liverpool, and awkwardly carries a 'You'll Never Walk Alone' tattoo on her skin.



While she played in red, she revealed she did it in tribute for her grandparents: "I got the tattoo in 2014 after my grandmother passed away.

"My grandparents are both from Wavertree in Liverpool but moved away during the war.



"It's just a commemorative thing to show that they are always with me."

She added: "I've been a Liverpool supporter since I was walking and since I knew what the game was.



"For me to be able to sign there and bring back my family name into the city where it originated has been an honour for me."

Foster-Inman also admitted it was a dream come true to sign for the club that she supports in 2020.

5 Foster shows off her tattoo after signing for Liverpool Women in 2020 Credit: Liverpool FC

'Everton Is About Core Values'

Re-joining Everton, she emphasised how much the city of Liverpool means a lot to her.



She said: "To represent the badge and to be in the city is what matters most to me. It is super exciting.

"Everton is about the core values of how hard you work and what it means to represent the badge.

"Everyone here is on the same beat and we all work hard. The team is very unified and it has a ‘never-say-die’ attitude.

She added: "It is awesome to be at this remarkable stadium, too. Goodison has always been a very important stadium to the club and its fans."



5 Goodison Park is now home to Everton Women Credit: Getty

Overcoming the crash

Since her first spell on Merseyside, Foster-Inman has endured a traumatic, life-altering event.

In 2021, the Canadian experienced a horrific car crash in Sweden that left doctors questioning whether she would ever walk again, let alone return to professional football.

She suffered an extensive list of injuries: Neck fractures, lower-back breaks, a broken cheekbone, partial tears in the knee and shoulder, and brain damage.



It was only upon returning to Liverpool for specialist assessment that doctors discovered her neck fractures were dangerously close to severing her arteries, which would have proved fatal.

Reflecting on her recovery, she said: "It was catastrophic, the doctor said he had never seen it this bad. He said, given the injuries I had, I should not have been breathing or talking on my own.

"Football just wasn't a thing, I was just trying to fight for a quality of life at this point.

"My personality and the way I come across is like I'm bulletproof. To see me at my worst like that, and being so vulnerable, was really hard for people.



"The first two weeks were really dark for me, I had no idea what was going to happen, but then I just became happy I was alive eventually.

5 Foster-Inman only made five appearances for Liverpool Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

"I survived something nobody should have, my injuries alone should have killed me. I had a euphoric feeling that I could not explain, but that also wore off.

"It got to the point where I was just angry and mad."

Rebuilding her WSL career

Everton became her first professional club following the incident as she bravely rebuilds her career.



She said: "I am happy playing now. When you are out of the game, it is hard to find your identity again. The accident gave me opportunity but took away my biggest passion. You lose that love for the game.

"For me to be back in the WSL, amongst the best of the best, I feel that love and desire. I'm being challenged and tested every day which is what I want.

"That challenge is what I was craving. I have that here. Back in a league where anything can happen."

5 This will be the Canadian's second spell with the Toffees, and she really likes the goalkeeper training staff at the club Credit: Everton Women



Exactly 731 days after the crash, she was back training between the sticks after being released by Liverpool at the end of her contract in 2022.

Reflecting on her departure from the Reds, she added: "Business is business. I was an asset that could not perform which is the cruel reality of football.

"At the end of the day, do I have hard feelings? No. I'm back in the city that I call home and my family is from. I have the opportunity to represent a club [Everton] which is just as established and historical.

"It is awesome. We are trying to grow the game; I have respect for both sides. I am honoured to be back playing."

Sports.title: Fikayo Tomori available for transfer as England star linked with move to ex-manager’s club
Sports.content:
Fikayo Tomori available for transfer as England star linked with move to ex-manager’s club

AC Milan have reportedly made Fikayo Tomori available for sale ahead of the final weeks of the transfer window.

Tomori is currently heading into his seventh season at San Siro having first joined on loan from boyhood club Chelsea in January 2021.

2 Tomori looks to be on his way out of Milan this summer Credit: Getty

The centre-back impressed during his debut campaign and his form sparked Milan to complete their £25million buy option.

However, despite starting 31 of their 38 Serie A matches last season, he appears to be on his way out of Milan.

Fabrizio Romano says I Rossoneri have named Tomori in their exit list.

The decision to make the 28-year-old available has come after talks between head coach Ruben Amorim and co-owner Gerry Cardinale.

Former Chelsea man Christopher Nkunku is also a potential departee alongside Youssouf Fofana.

Where could Tomori go?

With the summer transfer window closing on September 1, there is still time for Tomori to complete a move.

He boasts extensive experience at the top level having featured 214 times for Milan and won six caps with England.

Tomori is also a Serie A and Supercoppa Italiana champion, but now faces uncertainty ahead of the 2026/27 season.

Furthermore, he has only a year remaining on his contract, meaning a transfer may not be too expensive.

Tottenham Hotspur have had previous interest in the defender and considered a move in January 2025.

2 Tomori could reunite with Lampard amid links with a move to Coventry Credit: Getty

However, a move to north London looks unlikely as they have already signed centre-backs Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi.

Newcastle United were also keen on Tomori early last year, as well as West Ham United and Brentford.

A report from Italy has linked Premier League newbies Coventry City with a potential transfer.

Sky Blues boss Frank Lampard had Tomori on loan at Derby County before handing him his first-team breakthrough at Chelsea.

Tomori has made 81 appearances under Lampard, the second-most of any manager during his career behind Stefano Piolo on 142.

Liverpool, who recently signed Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona, have also been named as a potential destination.

Sports.title: Arsenal set to poach 16-year-old Liverpool wonderkid as Gunners continue shopping spree
Sports.content:
Arsenal have reached an agreement to sign England youth international striker Vincent Joseph from Liverpool.

The Gunners have agreed terms with the 16-year-old that'll see the teenager swap Merseyside for north London.

3 Teenage striker Vincent Joseph has swapped Anfield for the Emirates Stadium Credit: Instagram @vincent.joseph9

Arsenal are still yet to agree a settlement with Liverpool to sign Joseph.

And if the Premier League pair can't come to an agreement, then a tribunal will set a fee for the forward.

Joseph did not sign scholarship terms with Liverpool this summer following the expiration of his schoolboy registration contract.

It means that Joseph had been free to discuss a potential transfer to the Emirates Stadium.

Arsenal's youth drive

The move for Joseph maintains Arsenal's push to hoover up the brightest young talent English football has to offer.

The Gunners were left disappointed in their pursuit of Jeremy Monga from Leicester City, the teenage winger instead moving to Manchester City to reunite with Enzo Maresca.

However, Arsenal have agreed a deal to sign 16-year-old wonderkid Mylo Bernard from Crystal Palace.

Like Joseph, Bernard's schoolboy registration contract expired this summer, meaning he's been free to move elsewhere for a nominal fee.

Axel Donczew is also set to join the 2025/26 champions having become the youngest ever player to represent Cardiff's first team last October.

3 Arsenal missed out on Monga, who moved to Manchester City last month Credit: Manchester City

North London summer sales

The Gunners also completed the signing of Elijah Upson, the son of former centre-back Matthew, following his departure from rivals Tottenham.

Upson isn't the first player to depart the Spurs academy this summer.

Manchester United confirmed the arrival of Tynan Thompson from the capital outfit last month.

The winger was one of the club's brightest academy products, but Spurs sanctioned his sale for £8million, £4million of which was paid up front.

Spurs have cashed in on a number of young stars this summer, with Alfie Devine, Will Lankshear and Luka Vuskovic among those to depart.

Sports.title: Why Savinho missed Man City training amid Tottenham links
Sports.content:
Manchester City star Savinho missed training on Thursday due to illness, it's been reported.

City are gearing up for the Community Shield meeting with Arsenal at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

3 Savinho sat out Manchester City training ahead of their Community Shield meeting with Arsenal

However, the Athletic's Sam Lee confirmed the Brazilian sat out training in the lead up to the clash with the Gunners due to illness.

Jack Grealish was involved ahead of the meeting with the Premier League champions as the midfielder looks to make his first City appearance in over a year.

Erling Haaland, Rayan Cherki, Jeremy Doku, Nico O'Reilly, Elliot Anderson and Marc Guehi were also part of the squad for the Community Shield showdown.

Savinho's absence, albeit reportedly due to him being unwell, will further heighten speculation surrounding his future at the Etihad Stadium.

The former Girona man has been heavily linked with a move to Tottenham over the last 12 months.

Spurs failed in their pursuit of the 22-year-old last summer, and again at the turn of the year.

Spurs turn attention to attack

The north London side are hoping to land the Brazil international before the transfer window closes with the capital outfit set for a hectic end to the summer.

Spurs spent the first half of the window bringing in new bodies at the back as they signed Martin Dubravka, Andy Robertson, Marcos Senesi and Jan Paul van Hecke.

Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali both secured big-money moves to the club as they joined from West Ham and Newcastle, respectively.

3 Tonali is the marquee summer signing at Hotspur Way Credit: Tottenham Hotspur FC

Now, Spurs are looking to raise further funds in order to strengthen the attack.

Cristian Romero is on the cusp of a move to Atletico Madrid, while full-back Djed Spence is set to secure a switch to Inter Milan.

And Savinho isn't the only attacking player that Spurs have been linked with this summer.

Liverpool's Dutch forward Cody Gakpo is also believed to be on the club's radar.

However, Ben Jacobs outlined recently that Liverpool would rather keep than sell Gakpo.

"Liverpool’s preference is to keep (hold of Gakpo), that won’t change unless they add one if not two attack-minded players," Jacobs told Hawksbee & Baker last week.

"Then possibly towards the middle or the end of the window, maybe not today, tomorrow, but by the time we get into mid-August and beyond, if Liverpool get what they need in the market, Cody Gakpo’s position could change a little bit.

3 Tottenham are interested in signing Gakpo this summer Credit: Getty

"But, for now, it’s been described to me by sources as a ‘fool’s errand’ to negotiate with Liverpool for Gakpo now because they’re going to reject everything until such a point where they know one if not two players are going to come in.

"With Bradley Barcola being the top target and interest also in Ibrahim Mbaye amongst other players as well.

"And my sense is two would need to come in for Liverpool to change their stance, but Tottenham are serious about Cody Gakpo and that would in addition, according to my information, to Savinho, who Spurs are also working on.

"But before that one unlocks, it’s less about the finances and it’s more about Man City lining up a replacement."

Sports.title: Arsenal had ‘disgraceful’ offer for Premier League star instantly rejected as transfer decision looms
Sports.content:
Arsenal have expressed interest in signing Ezri Konsa, but their initial offer fell way below his true valuation.

That's the view of Gabby Agbonlahor, who outlined how much Aston Villa will want for the defender this summer.



3 Konsa sits top of the centre-back wishlist at Arsenal Credit: Getty

Konsa is understood to be the leading centre-back target for Premier League holders Arsenal amid injuries in the position.

William Saliba is out for an 'extended period' with a back issue that he picked up at the World Cup, whilst Jurrien Timber is still recovering from a groin injury.

It leaves Gabriel, Piero Hincapie and Cristhian Mosquera as their only options, though left-back Riccardo Calafiori can play at centre-back if needed.



Arsenal have made Konsa a target after his impressive performances for England at the World Cup, but appear to be far away from a deal.

How much did Arsenal offer for Konsa?

talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs gave an update on the potential move during Breakfast and confirmed that the Gunners are real suitors for Konsa.



"I'm keen to know what Gabby thinks because Villa have already been desecrated. There's no release clause as per Lucas Digne (£6million to Paris Saint-Germain and Youri Tielemans (£35m to Manchester United).

"But Arsenal are serious, despite links with Cristian Romero. He's off to Atletico Madrid, €40million (£34m).



"And Arsenal have actually already made a verbal offer, but this was a few weeks back and there was a huge gulf in valuation. My information is that Arsenal's valuation was in and around £35million..."

"Pardon?" a shocked Agbonlahor interjected before Jacobs continued: "And Aston Villa are looking for £60million, £65million and maybe, in this inflated market, even more...

"But ultimately, if you think about Arsenal, they'll be looking at some other defenders that have gone maybe outside the Premier League.

3 Agbonlahor could not believe that Arsenal had valued Konsa so low Credit: talkSPORT



"If you look at the Villa perspective - one, they don't want to sell, two, Jan Paul van Hecke (Brighton to Tottenham Hotspur), £52million, Maxence Lacroix (Crystal Palace to Chelsea), £52million.

"Ezri Konsa, England international, should ultimately be more, so it's just whether Arsenal are prepared to, effectively in their eyes, overpay.

"Whereas, Villa would say £60million, £65million. In this market, that's still decent value for money."

Agbonlahor then offered a Villa perspective as he explained: "I get it though, Ben, because he's got two years left.



"I've said it many times, his performances in the World Cup, his performances since his first day at Aston Villa... he'll be looking at (Marc) Guehi next to him, 'What's he earning at Manchester City?'

"Aston Villa can't get to those levels of £250k-a-week, maybe £300k-a-week, whatever he's earning, Guehi. He deserves that money.

3 Arsenal want to sign a new centre-back before the window shuts on September 1 Credit: Getty

"But Aston Villa will also say, 'Listen, we can't give you that money, but we need at least £65million, £70million'. £35million is a disgrace of an offer. If he had a year left, I'd get it, but not with two years left."



Jacobs then said: "By the way, when they made that offer, that was the perspective of Aston Villa. It was dismissed out of hand.

"So Arsenal are now coming back off the back of those talks, off the back of that gulf in valuation, and they have to decide whether they're going to significantly improve their offer

"And if they do, I think there's a fair chance it might happen. Jacobo Ramon at Como is another possibility, but Arsenal want to add a centre-back between now and the end of the window."

Konsa has made 286 appearances for Villa across all competitions and won the Europa League with them last season.



Formerly of Charlton Athletic and Brentford, a move to Arsenal would see him return to his birthplace of London.

Sports.title: How Manchester United are expected to line up for first 2026/27 Premier League match
Sports.content:
How Manchester United are expected to line up for first 2026/27 Premier League match

Michael Carrick will be forced to deal with an injury crisis heading into his first season as permanent Manchester United manager.

The Red Devils boss was promoted from his caretaker role in May after guiding the club back into the Champions League.

5 Carrick must juggle an injury crisis heading into the new season Credit: Getty

United finished third in the Premier League last term having lost just two of his 17 matches in charge.

His side will begin the new season away to newly-promoted Hull City on the opening weekend.

The two clubs meet at the MKM Stadium on Saturday, August 22 at 12.30pm, live on talkSPORT.

However, how will United line-up under Carrick when they take on the Tigers?

United injuries

The former midfielder will be without some key players heading into the first weekend of the season.

Several of those have been absent throughout pre-season, though, giving Carrick a chance to prepare for how he will cope until their return.

Matthijs de Ligt remains sidelined until September with a long-term back injury.

Meanwhile, Manuel Ugarte is set to miss the majority of the season after undergoing surgery on a knee injury suffered at the World Cup.

Kobbie Mainoo and Lisandro Martinez have both been unavailable so far this summer, with the latter forced off in the World Cup final with a thigh injury.

Benjamin Sesko also remains a doubt to face Hull due to the shin injury he suffered in May.

5 Sesko is one of eight players who could miss United's clash with Hull Credit: Getty

The Slovenia striker has yet to feature for United so far in pre-season ahead of their final outing against AC Milan on Saturday.

Mason Mount could miss out too after he was forced off against Paris Saint-Germain earlier this month.

Goalkeeping duo Karl Darlow and Tom Heaton are also currently absent, with the former still recovering from minor surgery.

How will United line-up on opening day?

Carrick has used his favoured 4-2-3-1 formation throughout United's pre-season schedule.

The shape was his preferred system as the Red Devils rallied to finish in the top four last term.

Fortunately for him, first-choice stopper Senne Lammens is fit after featuring for Belgium at the World Cup.

5 Summer signing Youri Tielemans is set to feature in midfield for United Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

The full-back positions are also at a full compliment, with Diogo Dalot and Luke Shaw likely to start the season on the right and left, respectively.

With Martinez and De Ligt both absent through injury, Carrick's centre-back options have taken a hit.

Whilst Ayden Heaven did impress when called upon last season, Harry Maguire and Leny Yoro are likely to get the nod against Hull.

Moving into midfield, summer signings Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have both featured heavily this summer.

The departure of Casemiro, paired with Mainoo and Ugarte's injury, means they are set to form a new-look pairing in the centre of the park.

In front of them, captain Bruno Fernandes remains United's creator-in-chief when it comes to the four-man attack.

5 Bruno Fernandes remains United's key man after a stellar season last term Credit: Getty

Amad Diallo has solidified his starting role on the right in pre-season, but there is more of a debate to be had on the left wing.

Full-back Patrick Dorgu has been converted into a wide forward under Carrick with three goals and one assist since his arrival.

Meanwhile, Marcus Rashford re-joined the squad ahead of Wednesday's friendly against Leeds United following his loan spell with Barcelona.

Despite that, Matheus Cunha can be expected to begin the season on the left flank for United.

As a result, Bryan Mbeumo will fill the void left by Sesko's enforced absence at centre-forward.

The 27-year-old, who did not go to the World Cup after Cameroon failed to qualify, scored 11 league goals during his first season with United.

Sports.title: UEFA ready to force Gianni Infantino exit and introduce rotating FIFA presidents
Sports.content:
Senior European football figures met in Salzburg ahead of the UEFA Super Cup to discuss the FIFA crisis, talkSPORT understands.

This included a meeting between UEFA president Alexander Ceferin and European Football Clubs chair Nasser Al-Khelaifi.

4 Al-Khelaifi has been Paris Saint-Germain's president since October 2011 Credit: Getty

The pair were pictured alongside each other as Al-Khelaifi's Paris Saint-Germain beat Aston Villa 2-1. And perhaps more significantly, Confederation of African Football president Patrice Motsepe was also in attendance.

talkSPORT understands constructive talks took place with Ceferin stressing the need for a change of leadership and governance within FIFA, including discussions at a pre-match lunch at Red Bull’s famed Hangar-7 museum.

Talks have been described by multiple sources as positive with UEFA intent on holding Infantino to account for the failure of FIFA Forward Enterprise, and accepting nothing less than his immediate resignation or the withdrawal of his candidacy ahead of March’s election.

talkSPORT understands Ceferin is even prepared to spearhead a vote of no confidence, that requires backing from 43 members to trigger an emergency vote, if Infantino continues to fight on.

It is viewed by many as a logical next step, and a more practical one than a boycott.

Which candidate is UEFA likely to back as Infantino's replacement?

UEFA are also prepared to back other candidates to stand against Infantino with CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani and Asian Football Confederation president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa potential options.

As of now, UEFA has not collectively recommend or supported any one candidate.

Al-Khelaifi would also be a popular choice as FIFA president, but said after PSG's win he's 'very happy' as PSG president.

Although Gianni Infantino has firm backing in Africa, and a few Asian federations on side, FIFA could essentially come to a gridlock without UEFA support. A boycott of FIFA competitions, potentially starting with the Under-20 Women's World Cup in Poland, is just one option UEFA are considering.

Refusing to engage with key FIFA meetings and even breaking away via a joint UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC venture are all under discussion.

4 Ceferin and Al-Khelaifi had plenty to discuss during the Super Cup Credit: Getty

The EFC is also a key player in all this as the body represents over 850 European clubs.

The EFC is a firm ally of UEFA, both generally and on the topic of how FIFA should be governed going forward.

Several insiders argue that any governance shake-up of FIFA should include a greater voice for clubs in global football matters. One topic to watch is whether the ‘E’ (European) in EFC turns to ‘W’ (worldwide) one day.

Another sub-plot is whether federations in Africa will remain universally in favour of Infantino. It was significant that Motsepe was also at the Super Cup.

Multiple sources have told talkSPORT his attendance was in part to discuss Infantino's future rather than solely to support African referee Omar Artan, who officiated the game after being banned from entering the USA to referee at the 2026 World Cup.

Speaking to Sky, Motsepe urged FIFA’s members to let the election decide Infantino’s fate, but stopped short of directly backing the under-pressure FIFA President.

4 Infantino's relationship with US President Donald Trump has proved extremely controversial Credit: Getty

"If you want to take him out, go for elections,” he said. “Let the 211 member associations decide. Do that and the vote will express whether they've got confidence in him or not."

Although no one has publicly come forward yet to run against Infantino, the November 18 deadline is currently viewed as secondary to a potentially more imminent vote of no confidence that could be triggered before it. Ceferin’s hope is that Infantino walks before this is necessary.

talkSPORT understands UEFA not only want Infantino gone, but to also rethink the FIFA presidency itself.

How could a new-look FIFA presidency operate?

This could see rotating presidents to dilute the office’s power, or even removing the title altogether and replacing it with a chair.

This could also see a series of vice-chairs providing further checks and balances, and a governance model not too dissimilar to the civil service.

Whereas Infantino pushed to align FIFA's commercial, operational and regulatory arms under one partly-privatised subsidiary, senior UEFA figures prefer a clear separation in each of these areas.

4 Infantino has, to date, refused to show any signs of quitting his post Credit: Getty

FIFA were approached for comment and pointed towards 'constructive and positive' talks in Morocco from select members of FIFA's leadership.

FIFA sources also reiterated their statement from last week which pointed to the fact, “The FIFA president was democratically elected by FIFA member associations and continues to serve with their mandate.

"Those who do not have the support of FIFA member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through FIFA's established democratic processes.”

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo unveils shock new look just days after marrying Georgina Rodriguez at intimate wedding ceremony
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has revealed an astonishing new hairstyle in the wake of his wedding to Georgina Rodriguez.

Gone is the black, slicked-back hair and in its place is a hairdo we never thought we'd see on him: a ginger buzz cut with a high skin fade.

The 41-year-old has been remarkably consistent with his look over the years but, with his fresh trim, it would now be hard to distinguish him from his old Manchester United team-mate Paul Scholes.

This could well be the haircut with which he passes his coveted 1,000 career goals mark.

The Al-Nassr star is on 976 goals for club and country and has a year left on his £488,000-a-day contract in Saudi Arabia.

Ronaldo was pictured returning to training, preparing for the season under new manager Ange Postecoglou alongside the likes of Sadio Mane and Kingsley Coman.

Cristiano Ronaldo debuted a bold new look as he returned to training with Al-Nassr

Just days ago he married Georgina Rodriguez in an 'intimate and private' ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, alongside their five children

CR7 finally broke his major trophy duck with Al-Nassr last campaign as they got their hands on the Saudi Pro League.

And on Tuesday he finally achieved his long-time dream of marrying Georgina in an 'intimate and private' ceremony with their five children present, a year after they first got engaged.

Ronaldo shared that he and Georgina had tied the knot after ten years together by sharing a snap of their wedding bands on Instagram.

A representative for Ronaldo also confirmed news of the union, saying: 'Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez were married today in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, and are now officially husband and wife.

'The ceremony was a private and intimate moment attended by their five children.'

Their wedding news came just days after it was thought the couple were set to marry in Funchal Cathedral, leading to thousands of fans gathering outside the church.

However, it was then revealed that the couple were not getting married there at all, and the ceremony turned out to be for an entirely unconnected Portuguese couple from Madeira called Fabio Ramos and Fatima Nicole Cunha Teixeira.

Georgina was working at a Gucci store in Madrid, earning £10 an hour, when she and Ronaldo met in 2016.

The Portugal star announced that he and Georgina had tied the knot by sharing a snap of their wedding bands on Instagram

The pair have two biological children, though she helps raise all five of his kids. Cristiano Jr. (pictured left) hugs his baby sister Eva while Georgina cradles Mateo on her lap, Cristiano (pictured right) holds his two daughters baby Bella and Alana Martina

Ronaldo, 41, is aiming to score 1,000 career goals and has a year left on his deal at Al-Nassr

Recalling their meeting, Georgina said: 'I was finally able to leave the shop to go home three hours later than I should have and as I was getting ready to leave Cristiano came in with his eldest son and some friends.

'Let's just say it was butterflies in my stomach.'

Cristiano would then pick Georgina up from work in his £1.5million Bugatti – after she had arrived at the shop on the bus.

'Many times he'd come after work', she said in her Netflix series I Am Georgina.

'He would come, I remember once, once in a Bugatti. My coworkers went crazy. They get there on the bus, and I would leave in a Bugatti. I mean people couldn't believe it.'

By December, she quit her job shortly after fans began crowding outside the store.

The following month, the pair made their first public appearance at The Best FIFA Football Awards, confirming speculation that they were a couple.

Cristiano and Georgina made their Instagram debut as a couple in March 2017 when the footballer posted a sweet snap of them cuddling on a couch.

Ronaldo proposed to Georgina last year with a huge diamond engagement, having previously said he 'waited' before popping the question

Georgina joked that the soccer star popping the question with an 'enormous' diamond ring was 'the least he could offer' after waiting for so long to propose

In June of that year, the footballer welcomed twins Mateo and Eva via surrogacy and then five months later, Georgina gave birth to their daughter, Alana Martina, in November.

The following month, Georgina posed for photos with her newborn daughter Alana for the cover of HOLA!

Revealing how they came up with the name for their daughter, she said: 'We both chose the name. Cristiano chose Alana and I chose Martina.

'We decided to give her both names that each of us chose. We thought it was even more special.'

In 2022, the couple welcomed twins; however, their baby boy tragically died during childbirth, while his sister, Bella Esmeralda, survived.

Opening up about how he and Georgina coped with the heartache of losing a baby, the footballer told Piers Morgan at the time: 'I feel that we always support each other. Sometimes it's like in a relationship you have good moments, bad moments it is part of the journey.

'But probably in that period, we consolidated it more, the relationship, but even in the worst moments you have to meet, you have to make the thing smooth.

'I learned so many things. I saw the other perspective of the life. My daughter, now who is three years old, she is the queen of the family, who made the house happy.

Cristiano met Georgina in 2016 after he saw her in the Gucci store where she was working

'Everything happens for a reason. I believe in that. So, we are a blessed family. I am proud of that.'

After nearly a decade together, fans were then desperate to know when Georgina and Cristiano would marry, with their family now complete.

However, in an interview with Marca last year, the Portuguese admitted he hadn't yet married Georgina because he hadn't felt the 'click'.

He said: 'I always tell her, "when we get that click". Like everything with our life, and she knows what I'm talking about.

'It could be in a year or it could be in six months or it could be in a month. I'm 1000 per cent sure that it'll happen.'

In August, the footballer finally popped the question with a giant diamond ring.

Fans speculated the pair got engaged the month before after the model shared pictures of a bridal-themed dinner, complete with 'C heart G' pillows, a six-piece band and stunning white flower arrangements.

She also wore a giant sparkler on her wedding ring finger, hinting at the pair's secret engagement.

Georgina gleefully shared the news on Instagram with a photo of her glitzy engagement ring. 'Yes I do. In this and in all my lives,' she wrote in a heartfelt caption.

Cristiano then revealed that two of his children inspired him to give Georgina a 'not-so romantic' and off-the-cuff proposal.

He revealed that he didn't plan to propose to the 'woman of his life' the night they got engaged, but it felt like the 'right time'.

'It was like 1am. My daughters were in bed sleeping,' the 41-year-old told Piers Morgan in part one of their new interview.

He said: 'One of my friends gave me the ring to offer Gio (Georgina) and as I was giving her the ring, my two kids come in and say "Daddy, you're going to give the ring to mum and you're going to ask her to get married."

'I said, "Wow, this is the right moment to say yes." It was the time. I knew that I was going to do it one day but I hadn't planned to do it then.

'Because my daughters said that and my friends were filming, it was what I wanted and I offered (the ring). I didn't (get on one knee) because I wasn't prepared but it was a beautiful moment. I made a speech.

'It was simple, I'm not a very romantic guy. Well, I am, but I'm not very romantic, not the kind of guy who brings flowers every week to the home. But I'm romantic in my way. It was beautiful and I knew that it's the woman of my life so I did that and I hope that I did it well.'

Asked about when they plan to tie the knot, the footballer joked: 'Not yet. We plan to do it after the World Cup with the trophy! But she is not the person that likes big parties. She doesn't like it. She likes private things. So I will respect these decisions.

'One thing that I love, she didn't care about the ring. She asked me if I was honest and I said, "I want you and I want to marry you." I didn't cry but I had tears on my eyes.'

Experts estimated that Cristiano splashed out an astonishing £1.5million on Georgina's engagement ring.

Sports.title: Chelsea still await bid for Enzo Fernandez despite looming deadline - as his suitors Man City agree to sell Tijjani Reijnders to Saudi Arabia: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Chelsea still await bid for Enzo Fernandez despite looming deadline - as his suitors Man City agree to sell Tijjani Reijnders to Saudi Arabia: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Chelsea wait on Enzo bid and let Badiashile go

Chelsea have still to receive any bids for Enzo Fernandez - 23 hours ahead of their self-imposed deadline.

Manchester City are interested but have been told to submit a written £120m offer by 5pm on Friday.

Chelsea are among the clubs to have checked on Monaco's Lamine Camara.

The principality club rejected an offer from Crystal Palace for 22-year-old Camara earlier this week.

Chelsea have also agreed a deal with Napoli for defender Benoit Badiashile.

The Italian side will take the French centre-back on an initial loan for £2.6m with a further £800,000 in bonuses. There is an option to buy for £23m and Napoli will cover the 25-year-old's salary in full.

Chelsea are yet to receive a bid from Enzo Fernandez after setting a deadline of 5pm on Friday

Leeds stay on Elvedi trail

Leeds United are continuing to work on a deal for Borussia Monchengladbach centre-back Nico Elvedi.

The Switzerland international, who can also play at right-back, emerged as an option prior to the World Cup when Leeds discussed a £7m offer and has given the go-ahead for a move to Elland Road.

The 29-year-old worked under Leeds boss Daniel Farke previously when he was in charge of Monchengladbach.

Elvedi has two years to run on his contract though it's understood he could leave for £8.2m.

Bye-bye Reijnders

Tijjani Reijnders has agreed to join Al Qadsiah from Manchester City.

The Saudi Pro League club coached by former Celtic and Liverpool boss Brendan Rodgers agreed a £52million fee with City.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed, Nottingham Forest had made a proposal earlier this month for the 28-year-old Netherlands international and Galatasaray had made an approach in recent days.

Tijjani Reijnders missed City's open training after Al Qadsiah made an offer for him

Spence set for Italian job

Djed Spence will travel to Italy ahead of his Inter Milan medical tomorrow.

Tottenham have agreed to sell the England international for £26million and his former club Middlesbrough hold a percentage sell-on of the profit.

Spurs paid £20m to buy Spence from Boro in 2022.

City reject fresh Rodri bid

Manchester City and Barcelona continue to discuss a fee for midfielder Rodri.

City have dismissed Barca’s latest offer of around £55m as they hold out for closer to £68m for the Spain captain.

Meanwhile, City forward Jeremy Doku has signed a new contract at the Etihad that will keep him at the club until 2031, with an option for a further year.

The Belgium international said : ‘This club means so much to me – I have developed as both a player and a person. I feel settled here, and I know I am improving every day because of the work the staff here do.

‘It’s hard to explain just how much this Club does to help players. I don’t take it for granted and it makes me better.

‘With Enzo here now I am really excited about the new season. His style of football is the kind we love, so that’s exciting for the players.

‘The City fans are also a huge reason I have signed this new contract. I feel their love and support, and it means the world to me. I want to focus of bringing them the success they deserve.’

Barcelona have had a fresh £55million bid for Rodri rejected by Manchester City

Galatasaray move for Martinelli

Galatasaray have made their move for Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli with a £38million offer.

However, the Brazilian is not inclined to leave for Turkey.

The 25-year-old is one of the players Arsenal are prepared to listen to offers for with a valuation around £50m.

Roma have also shown interest and it is understood Martinelli will only consider options from the strongest leagues.

Arsenal are re-evaluating options to strengthen their left hand side, they are also continuing discussions with Aston Villa for centre back Ezri Konsa with their latest proposal understood to be around £40m for the centre back.

Besiktas in the frame for £18m Willock

Besiktas remain in the frame for Newcastle United midfielder Joe Willock.

The 26-year-old has one year left on contract and is valued around £18m. Premier League sides have also shown interest while Besiktas had an offer rejected early this month.

Race for Nwaneri heats up

Interest is building in Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri who is considering his options and whether to depart this window.

A number of clubs, including RB Leipzig and other Premier League sides, have been looking to take the 19-year-old on loan or potentially a permanent basis after his disappointing spell with Marseille last season.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta praised the England U21 international after his return to pre-season training, saying: ‘Ethan has been really good, probably what happened on the field on his loan in Marseille wasn’t what was expected, and there was a lot of noise and change around the club.

‘But he looks different, a lot more mature, it’s incredible what six months and a different experience abroad can do to you - to be abroad on your own, to go through tough times and to witness that is a part of football you have to be good enough to cope with. I’m very happy with what Ethan has done in pre-season.’

Nwaneri joined Arsenal's academy aged eight and made his Premier League debut against Brentford in September 2022, becoming the youngest player to appear in the English top flight, at 15 years and 181 days old.

He has made 34 appearances for Arsenal and though only made nine appearances at Marseille, still managed to score two goals.

Pape Sarr a target for Al Ahli

Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr is emerging as a target for Al Ahli in the Saudi Pro League.

The 23-year-old will be allowed to leave if suitable offers arrive and has been the subject of interest from Brentford and Aston Villa as well as other European sides.

Spurs beat off strong competition to sign Sarr from Metz in 2021 and, while he has shown glimpses of what he is capable of, the Senegal international has been inconsistent overall, as have the majority of the squad in recent seasons.

The arrival of Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali mean his starting opportunities will be limited and he is open to exploring a move away.

Spurs are looking to wrap up the sales of Cristian Romero to Atletico and Djed Spence to Inter today.

They remain keen on Manchester City’s Savinho and Cody Gakpo of Liverpool. City’s Omar Marmoush is also on their list.

Villa expected to reject Arsenal offer for Konsa

Aston Villa were expected to turn down Arsenal’s initial proposal of £40million for Ezri Konsa, who is thought to be open to the move.

Villa are also looking to close deals for midfielder Joao Palhinha and left-back Matteo Ruggeri.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Ezri Konsa is said to be open to a move to the Premier League champions Arsenal

United youngster Williams joins Peterborough

Manchester United winger Ethan Williams has joined Peterborough United for a ‘sizeable’ undisclosed fee.

The 20-year-old, who was part of United’s pre-season tour of Finland, Norway and Sweden, has signed a long-term deal.

Williams had spent time on loan at League Two Cheltenham Town and Scottish Premiership outfit Falkirk.

He said: ‘I have enjoyed my time at [Manchester] United and it's always tough to leave a place like that, but there comes a time in your career where you have to make tough decisions to develop yourself and Peterborough is renowned for helping younger players.’

United’s deal also includes add-ons, a 50percent sell-on clause, a buy-back option and matching rights.

Tigers making moves in the market

Leeds United forward Joe Gelhardt has completed his medical at Hull City ahead of his £4.5million move.

He has agreed a four year contract with option for a further year. Wrexham and Rangers had also made efforts to sign the 24-year-old.

Meanwhile, Hull have formalised their interest in Everton midfielder Tim Iroegbunam with an offer understood to be in excess of £15million.

The 23-year-old has a year left on contract.

If it ain't So?

Brazilian side Palmeiras have signed Fabio So from Burnley.

The 18-year-old made 15 appearances in the U18 Premier League for Burnley, as well as a couple of appearances for the U21s. He left on a free transfer and has signed a contract until the end of January. The contract includes the possibility of an automatic renewal.

Portuguese midfielder So joined Burnley after being at Newcastle's academy.

Amorim's Milan exodus

AC Milan coach Ruben Amorim has decided Fikayo Tomori and Christopher Nkunku do not figure in his plans this season.

The former Chelsea players are available for sale along with midfielder Youssouf Fofana.

David Odogu, Pervis Estupinan, Santiago Gimenez and Philip Terracciano are also expected to leave.

Fikayo Tomori is one of eight AC Milan players who have been put up for sale by Ruben Amorim

Ge-Evan-noa

Brighton striker Evan Ferguson is a target for Genoa.

The Republic of Ireland international was on loan in Serie A at Roma last season, where he scored five goals in 22 appearances, and rivals Genoa would like him to return.

The 21-year-old has been hindered by niggling injuries and damaged his ankle in March but he is also attracting Premier League interest.

Reds youngsters on the move

Liverpool left-back Calum Scanlon is closing on a loan to Cardiff City.

The 21-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at Cardiff and they have been working hard to bring him back.

Scanlon has impressed on Liverpool's pre-season and attracted a number of enquiries.

League One Sheffield Wednesday, notably, made concerted effort to take the England U20 international to Hillsborough.

Liverpool midfielder James McConnell is a loan target for Championship side Preston North End.

A number of other Championship teams have enquired for the 21-year-old plus League One Leicester City.

Meanwhile, Arsenal are closing in agreement for 16-year-old striker Vincent Joseph who had decided to leave Liverpool last month.

Liverpool offered the teenager a scholarship but he declined and talks are ongoing over compensation.

The last teenager to leave Liverpool for another Premier League club was Isaac Moran. He left for Newcastle United earlier this year and a subsequent tribunal resulted in a seven-figure fee being payable to Liverpool with the settlement having the potential to reach £5m.

Sports.title: Revealed: What Diego Simeone told Julian Alvarez in showdown talks after Arsenal target reiterated his desire to leave Atletico Madrid
Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez has spoken to Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone for the first time since declaring that he wants to leave the club in order to 'fulfil my dream'.

The highly coveted Argentina forward, 26, is being tracked by several of Europe's biggest clubs, including Premier League champions Arsenal, LaLiga champions Barcelona and Real Madrid.

While representing Argentina at this summer's World Cup, Alvarez publicly declared his desire to leave Atletico, saying: 'I try to be an honest person. I spoke with the people at Atletico Madrid, and I think the best thing for everyone is a transfer. I want to fulfill my dream.'

Although reports have suggested Barcelona are Alvarez's preferred destination, Atletico have remained steadfast in their position that he is not for sale. Chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin said last month that the club would not entertain any offers for the striker, even in the region of £170m (€200 million).

Alvarez has a £428m (€500m) release clause and Atletico have already rejected a £129m (€150m) bid from Real Madrid.

The striker returned to pre-season training this week and, ahead of Wednesday's session, reportedly spent around 10 minutes speaking with Simeone at Atletico's Cerro del Espino training complex.

The striker returned to pre-season training this week after publicly declaring he would like to leave the club this summer in order to 'fulfil my dream'

Alvarez reportedly spent around 10 minutes speaking with Simeone (above) at Atletico's Cerro del Espino training complex, and reiterated his desire to leave during the conversation

According to reports, Alvarez, who is nicknamed La Arana, or 'The Spider', because of his Spider-Man celebration, reiterated his desire to leave during the conversation.

In response, Simeone is said to have restated the position he outlined publicly last week, namely that Atletico are planning for Alvarez to remain at the club.

'The situation is very clear, the club made a decision that Miguel Angel explained very well,' Simeone said. 'We are very happy with Julian. From a sporting perspective, we will help him to continue growing, to continue improving, and to give us back what he has given us in these two years, which was a great deal.'

The former Manchester City player, who won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina, joined Atletico in an £81.5m deal in 2024. He recorded 20 goals and nine assists in all competitions last season, while his 10 Champions League goals left him behind only Mbappe and Harry Kane in the scoring charts.

Back in April, Simeone said: 'I am not in Julian Alvarez's head. I suppose it is normal that an extraordinary player like Julian is wanted by Arsenal, Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona. It's normal because he's very good.'

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, meanwhile, has admitted there are 'very few players' in world football capable of immediately improving his starting XI, but insists the Gunners are still trying to make another marquee signing this summer.

Arsenal were heavily linked with Vinicius Jr before he signed a new contract with Real Madrid. They have, however, already secured the signing of Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes for £75m.

The former Manchester City player, who won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina, joined Atletico in an £81.5m deal in 2024

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, meanwhile, has insisted that the Gunners are still trying to make another marquee signing this summer

'I think for the margins to improve, there are very few players in the market that are available to do that and bring that to the club,' Arteta said after Arsenal's 1-1 draw with Como on Wednesday.

'Every time we have an opportunity to improve the squad and bring more quality and depth to the squad, we need to do that,' he said. 'We are actively trying to do so. The thing in the market is that it doesn't just depend on you. We are very clear on that.'

With more than two weeks remaining in the transfer window, there is still plenty of time for the situation to develop, while Arsenal may also benefit from Atletico's strained relationship with their LaLiga rivals.

One example came in June after Atletico rejected Real Madrid's £129m offer for Alvarez.

Real released a statement saying: 'Following the meeting of the board of directors held today, it has made an offer of 150 million euros to Club Atletico de Madrid for the federative rights of the player Julian Alvarez.

'After reviewing and evaluating the offer, Club Atletico de Madrid has expressed its gratitude for the proposal, made within the framework of the good relations between both clubs, and has rejected it, referring to the player's release clause.'

Atletico quoted the statement on X alongside a series of laughing emojis.

In a follow-up post, they added: 'You must have confused education with gratitude, but to leave no doubt: we don't thank you for anything.

'We neither study nor consider any offer for Julian. How could we not get along, when you make us laugh even more than Barcelona does.'

In a final swipe, Atletico posted: 'P.S. Taking advantage of the good relationship with your new president, let's see if you stop 'stealing' players from our Academy. Thanks a lot, @realmadrid!'

Sports.title: 'He'll be a big player for us this season': What's next for Brian Madjo, Aston Villa's great young hope - TOM COLLOMOSSE reveals 17-year-old in line to start season opener, why Unai Emery is perfect for him and what PSG goal means for England future
Sports.content:
Brian Madjo needed only 17 minutes to change Aston Villa’s outlook for the forthcoming season.

In that time he bullied Willian Pacho, one of the best markers in the world, and gave Marquinhos a fright, too. He had six attempts on goal and scored perhaps the most difficult, a far-post volley after outmuscling Pacho. Against Paris Saint-Germain, that would be a fair night’s work for any centre forward. For a 17-year-old making his competitive debut, it made the world sit up and take notice.

Even though they won the Super Cup, PSG were some way short of peak condition. Yet PSG are still PSG. For Madjo to make an impression like that was highly impressive and Daily Mail Sport understands he is leading the race to start the Premier League opener at Brighton on August 23, with Ollie Watkins not due back with the squad until this weekend.

Yet Madjo and fellow youngster George Hemmings, who was perhaps even more impressive, have lifted the mood around Villa Park.

Though supporters trust Unai Emery completely, they are frustrated at UEFA financial rules that have effectively forced them to sell Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne.

With Ezri Konsa also a target for Arsenal and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins returning to training only this weekend, there was creeping apprehension among some sections of the fanbase. For one night in Salzburg, Madjo’s performance blew that away.

Brian Madjo needed only 17 minutes to change Aston Villa’s outlook for the forthcoming season

He shrugged off the Paris Saint-Germain backline to fire in a euphoric equaliser for Aston Villa in the Super Cup on Wednesday night

What do his team-mates think?

Madjo joined Villa for £10million in January but his registration was initially blocked. The teenager is a Luxembourg international and FIFA’s regulations forbid overseas transfers of players under 18.

Yet Villa got the ruling overturned on appeal and Madjo, born in Enfield, north London, was cleared to play for them earlier this summer. Skipper John McGinn posted ‘English player allowed to play in England #freemadjo’ on his Instagram account – a sign of how well respected Madjo has become among the first-team squad.

‘He has obviously had to be very patient until he could play,’ said Tyrone Mings. ‘So, I think that says a lot about his character. He is very young and very strong. Clearly, mentally he is able to deal with setbacks.

‘He's a tough person to defend against. I think he is about 100kg (15st 11lb). He is a big old boy! He has got a very high ceiling. He is very difficult to play against.

‘He has trained with us for a long time. So when he eventually got his chance to play, he was ready. He knew our system, he knew how to press. I presume he watched a lot of Ollie Watkins and understood how we play. I’ve had a few chats with him in terms of what he’s about to go into.

‘The manager is big on what we do off the ball, probably more than what we do on the ball. Ollie’s a great person to watch, because of his work-rate and what he brings to the team.’

McGinn added: ‘He (Madjo) has been through a lot. He's not been able to play for six months to a year and he's handled that amazingly. He's kept himself in good shape. It would have been very easy for him to put his head down after those missed chances, but good strikers get themselves in those positions, and he's going to be a big player for us this season.’

He bullied Willian Pacho, one of the best markers in the world, and gave Marquinhos a fright, too, in the course of having six attempts on goal

Madjo scored twice in the first game of pre-season, a 5-0 win at Walsall last month, and also found the net against Real Sociedad and the Indonesia All Stars

Along with George Hemmings (pictured), who was perhaps even more impressive against PSG, Madjo has significantly raised the mood for Villa fans heading into the new season

What happens next?

Spotting the potential in Madjo and Hemmings, Emery deliberately loaded Villa’s pre-season schedule with fixtures. PSG were their seventh opponents of the summer programme, which Villa will complete against Borussia Monchengladbach on Saturday.

Emery wanted his younger players to grow accustomed to his style and tactical demands and on the evidence of the Super Cup, he was spot on.

Madjo has now scored five times in pre-season, with a brace against Walsall in the first friendly before also finding the net against Real Sociedad and the Indonesia All Stars.

Madjo’s rise makes it even likelier that Villa will listen to offers for Tammy Abraham between now and September 1, even though they paid £18million for the former England striker only seven months ago.

Daily Mail Sport understands Villa continue to track Nicolas Jackson and could still move in the closing hours of the window, though perhaps Madjo’s displays will make Emery wonder whether he needs two more forwards to compete with the 17-year-old.

Daily Mail Sport understands Madjo is leading the race to start the Premier League opener at Brighton on August 23

Even though he has represented Luxembourg three times, they were only friendlies, meaning Madjo is clear to play for England, for whom he has nine caps at Under-17 level

Even though he has represented Luxembourg three times, they were only friendlies, meaning Madjo is clear to play for England, for whom he has nine caps at Under-17 level. Expect him to be chosen for the forthcoming age-group squads.

He is remarkably strong for his age and loves a physical duel. Yet – quite understandably – there is work to do, particularly on his touch. The good news is that Emery has an outstanding track record of improving strikers and Madjo could not be in better hands.

As he prepares his team to meet Villa, you suspect Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler will hurriedly be making plans to contain this hugely exciting teenager.

Sports.title: Paul Pogba's wife hits back at claims he should retire, with 33-year-old set to have Monaco contract ripped up after yet another cruel injury blow
Sports.content:
Paul Pogba's wife hits back at claims he should retire, with 33-year-old set to have Monaco contract ripped up after yet another cruel injury blow

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Paul Pogba's wife has hit back after claims that her husband should retire from football, with Monaco set to rip up his contract.

The former World Cup winner and ex-Man United midfielder has been dogged by injuries in pre-season and multiple reports in France state that his agents are in talks with the club over a mutual termination, at Monaco's request.

Pogba had been trying to revive his career following a doping ban but only featured in six games last season while earning £44,000-a-week at the Ligue 1 side.

He suffered a knee issue after 45 minutes of pre-season and another nasty setback with a thigh injury last week. But with some fans suggesting his body can no longer tolerate playing at the top level, his wife Zulay, 33, defended her husband online.

She wrote: 'For all the people saying Paul should retire or he came back to football for the money, let me make this clear, the only one who knows when he will retire is God.

'And for the ones who say he came back for the money, trust me we are very good with money, thank God.

Paul Pogba's wife, Zulay (right), defended her husband aft

'Social media accepts everything. People can sit behind a screen and say whatever they want, insult someone, question their intentions and forget that there is an actual human being on the other side.

'For those questioning what he has left to prove, let me remind you he achieved the dream every footballer in the world grows up chasing, dreaming to have. He won the World Cup for his country.'

Zulay is a Bolivian model and influencer and the couple met in 2017 before getting married two years later. They have two sons aged seven and six together.

Pogba only returned to training last week after injuring himself in the first game of pre-season but sustained a thigh issue in a small-sided game and was scheduled for an MRI this week.

Daily Mail Sport understands he was offered to MLS clubs in America on Tuesday.

Pogba was allowed back into football in March 2025 after his doping ban was reduced on appeal.

He had already left Juventus after having that contract terminated by mutual consent in December 2024.

Pogba was emotional when he signed for Monaco last summer, describing his comeback as a second chance after what he called 'a time of darkness'.

The midfielder told Daily Mail Sport in 2024 that he discovered news of his reduced ban while preparing for a film premiere, adding: 'We went through hell. A time of darkness. But this is my second chance, I have to use it.'

Sports.title: Turkish giants Galatasaray make audacious move to sign Arsenal star Gabriel Martinelli - as Gunners set asking price for Brazilian
Sports.content:
Galatasaray have made their move for Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli with a £38million offer.

However, the Brazilian is not inclined to leave for Turkey.

The 25-year-old is one of the players Arsenal are prepared to listen to offers for with a valuation around £50m.

Roma have also shown interest and it is understood Martinelli will only consider options from the strongest leagues.

Arsenal are re-evaluating options to strengthen their left hand side.

They are also continuing discussions with Aston Villa for centre back Ezri Konsa with their latest proposal understood to be around £40m for the centre back.

Galatasaray have made their move for Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli with a £38million offer

Martinelli has been an ever-present at the Emirates over recent years after joining from Brazilian side Ituano as an 18-year-old in 2019.

Now 25, the forward has played 278 times for the club, scoring 62 goals, including 11 strikes in 53 appearances last season.

However, Martinelli struck just once in the Premier League, and of his 30 top flight appearances, only 11 were starts, with Mikel Arteta often preferring to use Eberechi Eze and Leandro Trossard on the left.

His most productive campaign was 15 league goals in 2022-23 and the Gunners have already added left-sided attacker Christos Tzolis this summer.

Speaking earlier this week on what we can expect from Arsenal over the rest of the transfer window, Arteta said: 'There is more that we want to do.

'Because every time we have an opportunity to improve the squad and bring more quality and depth, we need to do that.

'We’re actively trying to do so – the thing is, in the market, it doesn’t just depend on you, and we’re very clear on that.

'The will and the desire of the club is unquestionable, but we cannot promise that we’re going to do it because it doesn’t only depend on us.'

He added: 'For the margins to improve, there are very few players in the market that are available to do that and bring more quality to the club. But again, we’re actively looking to improve that and we’re going to try.'

Sports.title: Jon Rahm's Ryder Cup future is thrown into doubt AGAIN as European bosses tighten rules on LIV stars in major blow
Sports.content:
Jon Rahm’s Ryder Cup future is in doubt once more after European golf bosses tightened their regulations around players hopping between tours.

In a move that could prove decisive to Rahm’s existing deliberations over quitting LIV, sources say the DP World Tour has recently warned members of both circuits, like Rahm, of the likelihood of fines next season if they tee up in conflicting events.

Those sanctions were parked in 2026 for a cohort of LIV rebels, Rahm included, which was contingent on them agreeing to settle fines already accrued.

In Rahm’s case, that meant coughing up on a bill of close to £2million that he reluctantly paid after an ugly two-year stand-off in May, but having previously accused the DP World Tour of ‘extortion’, it will be intriguing to see how he reacts to the reintroduction of the measure in 2027.

It could be a moot point if he quits LIV at the conclusion of their 2026 season, with the Spaniard believed to be exploring the possibility of walking away two years before his contract expires.

Departing early would mean forfeiting a significant chunk of the £300m signing bonus he received in late 2023, but Rahm is acutely aware that the LIV of 2027, minus Saudi Arabian funding, will be a bleak proposition.

Jon Rahm is exploring the possibility of walking away from LIV two years before deal ends

If he chooses to stay with LIV, which at best will operate next year with only 10 tournaments and vastly reduced prize funds, he would risk six-figure fines from the DP World Tour each time he plays on the rebel circuit.

Much would then depend on him agreeing to pay the sanctions – not a foregone conclusion based on the aggression of his past objections – because a refusal could cost him his DP World Tour membership and eligibility for the 2027 Ryder Cup.

For LIV, keeping Rahm is potentially decisive to their hopes of finalising a provisional agreement with private equity backers to carry on beyond this season.

Sports.title: Arsenal and Liverpool in dispute over star, 16: Clubs heading for a tribunal after failing to agree compensation deal following player's decision to leave the Reds
Sports.content:
Liverpool and Arsenal are heading to a tribunal after failing to agree compensation for 16-year-old prospect Vincent Joseph.

The highly-rated striker, who had appeared for the club's U18s, decided to leave Liverpool last month despite the fact they offered the teenager a scholarship, which had to be signed by July 1. He declined the offer amid interest from the likes of Manchester United, Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund.

However, it is Premier League champions Arsenal who have won the race for the talented number nine's signature.

They have since been in talks with Liverpool over compensation but they have been unable to find common ground and amid the stand-off are now on a collision course for a tribunal to determine the fee due to the Anfield club.

The last teenager to leave Liverpool for another Premier League side was Isaac Moran.

The 17-year-old England youth international left for Newcastle United earlier this year and signed his professional contract in March. Again the clubs failed to agree on compensation and a subsequent tribunal resulted in a seven-figure fee being ordered payable to Liverpool with the settlement for the midfielder having the potential to reach £5m.

Arsenal and Liverpool are heading to a tribunal after failing to agree compensation for 16-year-old Vincent Joseph

Teenage striker Joseph decided to leave Liverpool last month despite being offered a scholarship

A tribunal ruled in February that Liverpool had to pay Chelsea £2.8m rising through add-ons to £4m after they signed Rio Ngumoha from the Blues

The battle for rising Premier League talents has become all the more costly and cut-throat in recent years.

Liverpool fended off strong interest from Manchester City, Arsenal and potentially Real Madrid to secure 16-year-old winger Josh Abe this summer. They also tied up dynamic attacking midfielder Erik Farkas despite City and United both trying plus clubs from Germany and Spain.

On the flip side, Liverpool previously angered Chelsea when they took Rio Ngumoha away from them last year.

The England international was regarded as the best player in his age group at Chelsea, but moved to Liverpool because he believed there was a better pathway to first-team football.

The 17-year-old left Chelsea in September 2024 and signed his first professional contract with Liverpool a year later.

The Professional Football Compensation Committee (PFCC) tribunal decided in February that Liverpool must pay £2.8m which could rise through add-ons to £4m while Chelsea will also be owed 20 percent of the profit if Ngumoha is sold.

The teenager scored on his Premier League debut in August aged 16 years and 361 days at the time, making him the youngest goalscorer in Liverpool's history.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
